===== SOURCE docs/methods.md | SHA256 3d7c9636b6db7c52d30518425896ca22ae10cd4895b3096551c49b803328366a =====
# Pilot methods — 0066

Status: revised after Claude Opus 5.5 review M0-initial; implementation review remains pending. Scope: descriptive pilot only, not all-trial atlas. OpenAI coordinates and implements; Claude independently reviews. No model fitting or causal claims. Preserve original pilot in analysis/0066.

## Data and eligibility

One trial, 10-fish/0066. Read track columns from actual schema. Natural keys (frame,id); network (frame,id1,id2). Require unique keys, finite mandatory numeric columns, positive lengths, identical time and segment across fish within a frame, constant fish set, and positive time increments. Split each fish at segment changes or nonunit frame jumps. Network endpoints must match tracks; no self links, duplicate links, nonpositive ray counts or nonfinite metrics. Explicitly compare network frame coverage to track coverage: a missing whole frame is unknown, not zero visibility, absent separate completeness evidence. For this pilot, restrict visibility analysis to covered frames and report count of uncovered frames. In covered frames, include zero-degree fish. Assert reported network distances match X/Y center distances within 1e-4 pixels for float64 or 1e-3 pixels if any source position/distance is float32; report dtypes and discrepancy; angular_size_deg = .36*n_rays within numerical precision.

## Units and smoothing

Image x right, y down. Keep pixel quantities and normalize descriptive distances/speeds by fixed trial median body_length L; no physical calibration. This is exploratory normalization, not a predictive training transform. Pilot temporal filter: Savitzky–Golay cubic, windows 7,11,15 frames (~0.23,0.37,0.50 s). Primary w=11. Derivatives use actual within-block dt, which must be regular within tolerance. Exclude w//2+1 points at both ends so known noisy join-adjacent samples do not enter retained derivative windows; require blocks longer than twice this margin; do not bridge gaps. Before unwrapping, flag adjacent samples with abs(wrap(delta ANGLE)) > pi/2. Exclude their entire SG support from turn rate and slip; omit affected frames from polarization. Report head-to-tail axis disagreement separately as QA, without silently treating bent midlines as heading errors. Unwrap ANGLE within blocks before deriving turn rate. These are noncausal exploratory derivatives. Sensitivity comparisons use common eligible rows across windows.

## B1 individual movement

v = derivative of X,Y; a = second derivative; speed=norm(v)/L; acceleration magnitude=norm(a)/L. Body turning = derivative of unwrapped ANGLE (rad/s), positive clockwise in image coordinates. Slip = wrapped(atan2(vy,vx)-ANGLE), rad; exclude speed <0.5 L/s and heading-jump-affected windows. Report eligible fractions. Evaluate slip and circulation eligibility at .25,.5,1.0 L/s. Estimate an illustrative derivative-noise scale from raw-minus-smoothed position residuals and SG coefficient norms; residuals include true movement and are correlated, so this is a sensitivity diagnostic, not a calibrated tracking-error model. Primary plot: speed and turn-rate distributions and speed sensitivity, weighted equally across eligible fish-frames. Descriptive percentiles, no independent-sample confidence intervals.

## B2 posture

Use only midline indices 0..20, not eyes 21..22. For each row, let normalized arc coordinate u=linspace(0,1,21) per source equal spacing. Fit cubic x(u), y(u) by least squares on indices 7..13; evaluate at u=.5. Curvature k=(x' y'' - y' x'')/(x'^2+y'^2)^(3/2); exclude derivative norm <=1e-8 pixels per u. Positive means clockwise head-to-tail tangent rotation in y-down coordinates. When the head-to-tail tangent is opposite the body heading, this is concavity toward fish-left; it does not share the positive-right-turn convention. Do not infer turn direction from curvature alone. Report k in 1/px and k*L. Compare neighborhoods 5,7,9 points on common eligible rows. Posture figure: distribution of k*L plus midlines at predefined temporal quantiles .1,.5,.9 for the lowest ID, translated to head and rotated into body-heading coordinates; examples are illustrations, not typicality claims. Geometric curvature can reflect tracker noise and is not a direct force or intent measurement.

## B3 collective organization

P=norm(mean_i([cos ANGLE_i,sin ANGLE_i])). RMS spread=sqrt(mean(norm(r_i-centroid)^2))/L, using SG-smoothed positions; nearest-neighbor distances use raw positions. Centroid speed=norm(mean_i v_i)/L, only frames with all fish valid.

Circulation: r_i is displacement from instantaneous SG-smoothed position centroid, u_i=v_i-mean_j v_j, with all v_j required valid. Eligible fish have norm(r_i)>1e-6 L and norm(u_i)>=0.5 L/s. C=abs(mean_i cross(rhat_i,uhat_i)) on eligible fish, where cross in y-down coordinates is rx*uy-ry*ux. Emit C only if at least 80% of fish eligible; save eligible fraction. Also save signed mean circulation. An illustrative iid isotropic-direction reference is E|mean cross| approximately 1/sqrt(pi*n_eligible); centroid-relative velocities are dependent, so this reference is not a calibrated null or significance test. Do not identify low/moderate C with milling from this alone. This measures coherent circulation in centroid-relative motion; pure translation has undefined C, not zero. P does not require velocity and is available on complete frames outside the conservative SG-support heading-jump mask. Figure: P,C,spread over time (lines broken at missing/segment joins) plus P vs C only valid frames. Low P does not establish disorder.

## B4 spatial relations

All ordered focal-neighbor pairs per complete finite frame, excluding self. The occupancy map uses raw headings including SG-support and reverse-motion candidate rows, with this limitation disclosed; no head-tail correction is inferred automatically. Delta=r_j-r_i uses raw tracker positions. On maps horizontal=forward, vertical=fish-right increasing down; posture uses the same convention. Forward=dx*cos(theta_i)+dy*sin(theta_i); right=-dx*sin(theta_i)+dy*cos(theta_i). Scale by L. Nearest distance=min_j norm(delta)/L. Relative-heading distributions are deferred; no relative-heading claim is made in this pilot. Primary body-frame heatmap uses bins fixed [-10,10] L in each axis, 40x40 bins; colors are mean neighbors per eligible focal observation per square L. Normalize by ALL eligible focal observations, not just pairs inside the view; report displayed pair fraction. Spacing distribution includes all finite nearest distances. No wall-based claims until arena geometry is validated. Map asymmetry is occupancy, not attraction or avoidance.

## B5 reconstructed visibility

Only covered frames as above. Out-degree of observer id1, including zero-degree fish. Visible fraction=degree/(N-1). Directed reciprocity=number of directed edges with reverse present / number of directed edges; report edge-weighted pooled value, not ambiguous mean. Angular size distribution across edges. Persistence is deferred to later pilot extension, to avoid implying disappearance at gaps. Primary figure: visible-degree histogram, per-frame mean degree time trace, angular size distribution. Do not equate visibility with influence. Table direction id1 sees id2, later GNN messages id2 to id1.

## Video check and representative selection

Attempt overlays at tracked frames nearest the 10th,50th,90th time quantiles. Record exact frame IDs, compare video frame i and i-1 because source reports one-frame ambiguity, show both if ambiguous. Overlay midlines and IDs; record visual assessment, not a numeric alignment accuracy without measurement. No tank-wall geometry is inferred in this pilot.

## Tests and output provenance

Before real runs: analytic constant speed and acceleration; signed analytic turn across wrapping; segment gap exclusion; parallel headings P=1; symmetric tangential circle C=1; pure translation C undefined; straight midline k=0; sampled circular arc k approximately 1/R with sign in y-down; known forward/right neighbor position; directed graph containing zero-degree node; invalid/dangling inputs rejected. Reviewer independently reasons about analytic results; executed test logs are supplied, but tool-free Claude review is NOT independent execution.

Save environment lock, config, source snapshot hashes, raw input SHA256 and ZIP CRC provenance, commands, filters/counts, summary CSVs, five figures, JSON metrics and report. Mark raw measurements/derived/reconstructed evidence distinctly. All quantitative results pilot-only. No confidence intervals or causal inference. Frozen source snapshot for each Claude review; changes after review require new hashes and review.

## Sustained heading QA after implementation review

Report each >pi/2 contiguous heading step with fish ID, segment and frame. Separately flag speed-eligible rows where abs(wrap(travel direction minus body heading))>pi/2, before heading_valid masks, and report the longest contiguous run per fish. Break runs at frame gaps/segment changes. These flags can reflect backward swimming, tracking defects or derivative error; they do not prove a head-tail flip. Existing axis agreement cannot exclude simultaneous heading/pose reversal. Preserve candidate intervals and disclose them as unresolved rather than silently correcting headings. Circulation/alignment plots are explicitly conditioned on relative-motion eligibility, not a joint distribution of all recorded frames.

===== SOURCE docs/source-README.md | SHA256 42c1a655bc1b5ce2b294175f0ae1516e811564b3cbe3d5ed4e2560a27eaa307c =====
# Golden shiners: tracks with posture, for social-force inference

Free-swimming golden shiners (*Notemigonus crysoleucas*) in groups of 10, 30, 70 and 151,
filmed from above. There are ten trials, about 13 minutes each at 29.97 frames per
second. For every fish in every frame the tables give a position, a measured heading,
a 21-point body midline and both eye positions. Identities are continuous through each
trial.

Source: Davidson JD, Sosna MMG, Twomey CR, Sridhar VH, Leblanc SP, Couzin ID (2021).
Collective detection based on visual information in animal groups. *J R Soc Interface*
18: 20210142. doi:10.1098/rsif.2021.0142. The raw data is on Dryad,
doi:10.5061/dryad.sbcc2fr2h, under CC0 1.0, and so is this derivative.

## Files

```
shiners-social-forces/
  README.md                       this file
  dataset.yaml                    mosaic manifest (its notes field repeats the conventions below)
  tracks/convert-schooltracker_midline_fov_h5.1.0-8c8f6ad206/
      <group>__<trial>.parquet    one table per trial: positions, heading, posture (4.3 GB)
  features/visual-network__from__tracks/0.1-65625b7549/
      <group>__<trial>.parquet    one table per trial: who sees whom, per frame (2.8 GB)
  media/joined/<hash>.joined.mp4  one video per trial, segments joined (1.4 GB)
  media_raw/150-fish/150-fish/calibrated_lowres30.25.mp4    the 150-fish video
```

| group | trials | fish | frames per trial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `10-fish` | 0066, 0105, 0126 | 10 | about 24,580 |
| `30-fish` | 0084, 0115, 0120 | 30 | about 24,580 |
| `70-fish` | 0103, 0107, 0124 | 70 | about 24,570 |
| `150-fish` | 150-fish | 151 | 17,999 |

The 150-fish trial has 151 tracks. Its directory name and its track count are both kept
as they are in the source.

## Reading a table

You need only pandas and pyarrow; mosaic is not required.

```python
import pandas as pd, glob
path = glob.glob("shiners-social-forces/tracks/*/10-fish__0066.parquet")[0]
df = pd.read_parquet(path)            # one row per fish per frame
# positions of all fish, frame by frame, as an array (frames, fish, 2):
wide = df.pivot(index="frame", columns="id", values=["X", "Y"])
```

## Columns

| column | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `frame` | video frame number (see "Time and gaps") |
| `time` | seconds, `frame / 29.97` |
| `id` | fish identity, constant through the trial |
| `segment` | which recording segment the row comes from (0-6) |
| `X`, `Y` | body centre, in pixels: the mean of the 21 midline points |
| `ANGLE` | heading in radians, `atan2(dy, dx)` in image coordinates |
| `body_length` | visible body length in pixels |
| `poseX0..20`, `poseY0..20` | body midline in pixels, from 0 = head to 20 = tail tip |
| `poseX21`, `poseY21` | left eye, in pixels |
| `poseX22`, `poseY22` | right eye, in pixels |
| `group`, `sequence` | group size and trial |

## Conventions

- **Units are video pixels.** The image is 1920 × 1032 px (1890 × 1080 for the 150-fish
  trial), and **y points down**. A fish's right side is the heading rotated by +90°
  in these coordinates. No pixel-to-centimetre scale is recorded in the source data;
  `body_length` (about 38 px) is the natural length unit.
- **The heading is measured**, from the tracker's body-axis fit, not derived from the
  direction of travel. It differs from the direction of travel by a median of 3.5°.
- **The midline** consists of 21 points at equal arc spacing along the body. Its total
  length equals `body_length`. Checked against the video, the midline points lie a
  median of 0.5 px from the dark centreline of the fish.
- **`body_length` is half the tracker's raw value.** The tracker's value overshoots the
  visible fish about two-fold. In the nine 10-, 30- and 70-fish trials the halved value
  matches the visible fish in the video. The same factor of 0.5 is used for the
  150-fish trial, which was filmed with a different camera setup (1890 × 1080 video).
  There the visible fish measures about 15% longer than `body_length`. No per-trial
  correction is applied, so the midline and `body_length` of that trial are about 15%
  short. The midline shape still fits the fish (median lateral offset 0.5 px).

## Time and gaps

Each trial was recorded as seven consecutive segments of about 2 minutes. The tracker
skipped one video frame per segment, so **one frame is missing at every segment join**.
The trajectories confirm this: extrapolating each fish's velocity across a join gives
about 2 frames elapsed. `frame` counts video frames, so at a join it jumps by 2 and
`segment` increments.

The positions next to a join are also noisier. The first tracked frame of a segment
deviates about 1.5 px from a smooth path, against about 0.5 px elsewhere, and the last
frame before a join about 0.8 px. A velocity computed with the correct time step is
therefore still about 1.2 times too high across a join, and an acceleration shows a
spike there.

**For anything that takes time derivatives, treat each segment as its own continuous
recording.** Do not difference across a join:

```python
for (fish, seg), track in df.groupby(["id", "segment"]):
    t = track["time"].to_numpy()
    vx = np.gradient(track["X"].to_numpy(), t)  # never spans a join
```

That gives 7 continuous pieces of about 2 minutes per trial, with identities carried
through.

## Identity

Within a segment, identities come from the tracker. Each segment numbers its fish
independently, so identities across a join were **reconstructed**. Every fish in the
first frame of a segment was matched to a fish in the last frame of the previous segment
by a global position assignment, with one frame of motion between them. The matched
distance is typically a few pixels, while the next-nearest candidate is typically more
than ten times further away. In rare cases two fish cross exactly at a join, and the
assignment between them is then less certain. Over all joins, 12 of 1,980 fish had a
runner-up nearer than their own match.

`detected` is 1 for every fish in every frame of the source, so the tables have no gaps
within a segment.

## Visual networks

`features/visual-network__from__tracks/0.1-65625b7549/<group>__<trial>.parquet` lists,
for every frame, which fish each fish can see. One row is one directed link: fish `id1`
sees fish `id2` in frame `frame`. **A pair that is absent from a frame is not visible in
that frame.**

| column | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `frame` | as in the tracks |
| `id1` | the observer |
| `id2` | the fish it sees |
| `n_rays` | rays (of 1000 per eye) whose first hit is `id2` |
| `angular_size_deg` | the angle `id2` covers in `id1`'s view, `n_rays * 360 / 1000` |
| `distance` | body-centre distance, pixels |
| `perspective` | 0 if `id1 < id2`, else 1 (mosaic's pair-table convention; ignore it) |

The method is the ray casting of Davidson et al. (2021). Each fish is a four-sided
outline: head, right eye, tail tip, left eye. From each eye, 1000 rays are cast
evenly over 360 degrees, and each ray stops at the first outline it meets. Fish `id1`
sees `id2` when at least one ray from either eye hits `id2` first. Each eye covers its
own side plus 12.5 degrees across the midline, which leaves a 25-degree blind wedge
behind the fish. Fish of the same group block each other's view; there is no partial
transparency.

To get the network of one frame as an adjacency matrix:

```python
net = pd.read_parquet("features/visual-network__from__tracks/0.1-65625b7549/10-fish__0066.parquet")
f = net[net.frame == 1000]
A = pd.crosstab(f.id1, f.id2).reindex(index=range(10), columns=range(10), fill_value=0)
```

On average a fish sees 6.8 of the other 9 fish in a 10-fish group, and 85 percent of
links are reciprocated.

## Videos

Each trial's seven segments are joined into one video. **Frame `i` of the joined
video is track frame `i`**, counted from 0. Frame 0 of each segment has no tracks
(see "Time and gaps"), but the video keeps it.

| trial | video |
| --- | --- |
| 10-fish/0066 | `media/joined/e29d6495a5.67dcc35d06.joined.mp4` |
| 10-fish/0105 | `media/joined/b98be8fc26.67dcc35d06.joined.mp4` |
| 10-fish/0126 | `media/joined/e1d5eec202.67dcc35d06.joined.mp4` |
| 30-fish/0084 | `media/joined/9d17691756.67dcc35d06.joined.mp4` |
| 30-fish/0115 | `media/joined/84afa71461.67dcc35d06.joined.mp4` |
| 30-fish/0120 | `media/joined/3469428553.67dcc35d06.joined.mp4` |
| 70-fish/0103 | `media/joined/80b84cbbf1.67dcc35d06.joined.mp4` |
| 70-fish/0107 | `media/joined/bc886afc4c.67dcc35d06.joined.mp4` |
| 70-fish/0124 | `media/joined/7fec52a075.67dcc35d06.joined.mp4` |

The joined videos are **AV1**, re-encoded from the original MPEG-4 at near-lossless
quality (CRF 14). VLC and current browsers play them. In Python, read frames with PyAV
(`pip install av`), because OpenCV's pip builds often cannot decode AV1. The original
segment videos are on Dryad.

Frame alignment between the tracks and the video is accurate to about one frame.
Measured against the video, the mapping is between frame `i` and frame `i - 1`. The
tracks themselves do not depend on this.

===== SOURCE docs/workflow/reviews/comparison-plan/review.md | SHA256 9426e25c94dd7ed3ccf7e53461298ed0bf89cca1e99bc9c20d2eeea212ad9dc1 =====
# Review: all-trial descriptive comparison plan

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUESTED.** The plan is sound in structure. Trials are the replicate, frame CIs are not passed off as between-trial uncertainty, C is not corrected by its iid reference, and there is no milling classifier or causal language. The changes below fix selection effects that vary with N and an incomplete treatment of the N=151 length bias. Without them, cross-N patterns could come from the method rather than the fish. All the fixes are descriptive and need no model, classifier or test.

---

## Material findings

### M1. Excluding whole frames for one fish's heading jump biases P by N
`docs/methods.md` (B1/B3) drops a whole frame from polarization if any fish's SG support touches a heading jump. If the per-fish-frame exclusion probability is *p*, frame retention is about (1−p)^N:

| p | N=10 | N=151 |
|---|---|---|
| 0.001 | 0.99 | 0.86 |
| 0.01 | 0.90 | 0.22 |

Excluded frames are probably not random. They are likely enriched for fast turns, crowding and tracking stress. So P at N=151 (and to a lesser degree N=70) would describe a progressively more selected subset of time.

**Fix:**
- Report the frame-retention fraction for P per trial, broken down by exclusion reason.
- Add a sensitivity analysis that drops only the affected fish rather than the whole frame. Record n per frame, and compare medians on the common frame set.
- If the cross-N ordering of P differs between the two masks, report the pattern as unresolved.

### M2. P has no finite-n reference saved, unlike C
For iid uniform headings, E[P²] = 1/n exactly and E[P] ≈ √(π/(4n)). That gives roughly 0.28, 0.16, 0.11 and 0.072 for n = 10, 30, 70 and 151. A raw decline of P with N is therefore expected even with no change in behavior.

**Fix:**
- Save √(π/(4n)) per frame next to P, with the same "illustrative, not a null" label used for C.
- State in the narrative that any P-vs-N statement must be read against this reference.
- Do not subtract or divide by it, matching the C rule.

### M3. The N=151 length scenario covers too few outputs
Every output scaled by L shifts under L×1.15:

- **Simple rescales:** spacing and spread divide by 1.15; body-frame density per L² multiplies by 1.15² ≈ 1.32; centroid speed and k·L also shift.
- **Outputs that need recomputation:** anything with a speed-dependent cutoff, i.e. slip eligibility, C/P eligibility, and the threshold sweep.
- **Not fixable by rescaling:**
  - **Curvature.** The source says the midline is about 15% short yet still fits the shape. That could be uniform scaling or truncation (for example, a missing tail tip). If it is truncation, midline indices 7..13 are not the anatomical midpoint, so k is not comparable to the other trials.
  - **Visual network.** It was ray-cast from the stored, too-short outlines. That plausibly lowers occlusion, raises degree and visible fraction, and shrinks angular sizes.

**Fix:**
- Apply the L×1.15 scenario to all L-normalized outputs, recomputing those with eligibility cutoffs.
- Mark N=151 curvature and network metrics as length-biased in an unknown direction or size, with no available correction.
- Exclude N=151 from any claim that curvature or visibility varies with N.

### M4. Other N=151 confounds need a statement
The N=151 trial differs in more than length:

- **Duration:** 17,999 frames (about 10 min) vs about 24,580 (about 13.7 min). If behavior drifts within a trial (acclimation), comparing the full duration mixes in a time-window effect.
- **Time base:** `time = frame/29.97` is a converter convention. The raw video name `calibrated_lowres30.25.mp4` does not confirm the frame rate, and the frame rate cannot be checked from the tracks. Speeds, turn rates and the BL/s thresholds all depend on it.
- **Segment structure:** this is a single unjoined video, so the seven-segment join structure may not apply. The plan already says to use actual segments.
- **Chirality:** a different camera or calibration could flip the image.

**Fix:**
- Recompute the smaller trials' summaries on their first 17,999 frames as a matched-duration sensitivity.
- Record the 29.97 fps assumption for N=151 as unverified.
- Do not compare signed C (direction of rotation) across cameras.

### M5. Threshold-intersection comparison: say what it actually isolates
Frame eligibility is monotone in the threshold. Reaching ≥80% of fish at 1.0 BL/s implies reaching it at 0.5 and 0.25. So the "intersection of eligible frames" is exactly the 1.0-eligible frame set, a strongly selected high-relative-motion subset. Holding fish fixed as well makes C identical across thresholds, which is trivial.

**Fix:** report two explicit components:
1. **Frame-selection effect:** C at a single threshold, computed on each threshold's frame set.
2. **Fish-composition effect:** different thresholds compared on the common (1.0-eligible) frame set.

Label the common set as "high relative motion frames", not as representative.

### M6. Pre-specify what counts as a cross-trial pattern
The plan bans significance tests but does not define "consistent across trials". That leaves room for post hoc reading of 3+3+3+1 points.

**Fix:** before results are viewed, fix a descriptive criterion. For example: "monotone in N" means every trial at a smaller N lies on the same side of every trial at the next N, so the ranges do not overlap. Anything else is reported as overlapping or inconsistent. N=151 can be at most "consistent with" the trend and never establishes it.

---

## Reasoning checks (static, by me)

- **Leave-one-out identity.** v_bar_all = (v_i + (N−1)·v_bar_other)/N, so v_i − v_bar_all = ((N−1)/N)·(v_i − v_bar_other). This is correct, and the same identity holds for r_i about the centroid. Directions are unchanged, so with the same eligible set, C under leave-one-out equals C under the all-fish mean.
  - Only eligibility changes. The secondary threshold 0.5·(N−1)/N is 0.45, 0.483, 0.493 and 0.497 BL/s across N, so the diagnostic matters mainly at N=10. The "diagnostic, not correction" framing is correct.
- **C reference.** For iid uniform directions, E[sin²] = ½, so E|mean| = 1/√(πn). This is correct. It must be evaluated per frame with that frame's n_eligible, as the plan says. Σr_i = Σu_i = 0 makes this anti-conservative or biased in an unknown direction at small N, so the "not calibrated" wording is correct.
- **Eligibility counts.** ceil(0.8N) gives 8, 24, 56 and 121 (121/151 = 0.801). Recording eligible fractions is adequate.
- **Replication framing** (one point per trial, equal weighting, ranges, no frame-based CIs) is correct.

## Checks not executed

- No code, tests, configs or outputs were run or inspected beyond the supplied text. I did not verify that `configs/comparison.json` drives the implementation.
- Per-trial schema, segment structure, frame gaps, fish counts and body_length medians were not verified.
- Heading-jump exclusion rates were not measured, so the size of M1 is unknown.
- The N=151 frame rate, image orientation and midline truncation vs scaling were not verified.
- Network completeness, adjacency bitset correctness and duplicate handling were not verified.
- No results or draft narrative were supplied. The required implementation/results review is still pending and is separate from this plan verdict.

===== SOURCE docs/workflow/reviews/comparison-implementation/review.md | SHA256 491be78493dab7c7b46e703fb9b3c12f4afd4107c68c846be3336973d14445d8 =====
# Independent implementation review: all-trial comparison code

## Verdict: **PASS** (implementation snapshot only)

This is not a results or scientific-release approval. I found no mathematical or implementation error that requires a rerun.

The items below are non-blocking. Two of them (N1, N2) should be dispositioned before the narrative review, because they affect how saved tables are read rather than what they contain.

All statements below come from my static reading of the supplied source. The test outcomes are the implementer's report (`reports/test-results-comparison.txt`), not my execution.

---

## Static verification of the requested focus areas (no blockers found)

**1. Coordinate and sign definitions**
- Body-frame right is `-dx·sinθ + dy·cosθ` (`metrics.spatial`). At θ=0 this gives right = +dy, which is down in y-down image coordinates. That matches the source convention ("right = heading rotated +90°").
- The circulation cross product is `rx·uy − ry·ux` (`metrics.collective`), consistent with `docs/methods.md`.
- Curvature (`metrics.curvature`):
  - The arc parameter is `u = i/20 − 0.5`, so the fit is evaluated at index 10 (u=0).
  - The first and second derivatives are `c1` and `2·c2`, which is correct for a monomial basis at u=0.
  - The κ formula is parametrization-invariant, so the u-scaling does not matter.
- Signed C is labelled image-coordinate and not for cross-camera chirality comparison.

**2. Finite-N references**
- C: with iid uniform directions, sin φ has variance ½, so the mean has σ² = 1/(2n). Then E|Z| = σ·√(2/π) = 1/√(πn). The code computes this per frame with `counts[valid]`. Correct.
- P: the resultant is Rayleigh with per-component σ² = 1/(2n), so E[R] = σ·√(π/2) = √(π/(4n)).
  - In `heading_selection` the primary reference uses n=N, valid because primary P requires all fish valid.
  - The affected-fish-only reference uses the frame's `n_valid`. Correct.
- Neither reference is subtracted or divided out anywhere, including in the plots.

**3. Metric eligibility and denominators**
- 80% eligibility uses `eligible.mean(axis=1) >= 0.8`. The boolean sum is an exact integer, so k/N is correctly rounded and the boundary cases (8/10, 24/30, 56/70) compare as intended.
- For N=151, 121/151 passes and 120/151 fails, as expected.
- Eligible fractions are NaN rather than 0 when any velocity is undefined.

**4. Threshold nesting** (`threshold_frame_selection`, `common_cohort_summaries`)
- Per-fish eligibility at 1.0 implies eligibility at 0.5, which implies eligibility at 0.25. So the frame sets are exactly nested.
- The threshold "common" set is therefore exactly the 1.0-eligible set, as the plan states.
- The two components (fixed-baseline C on each threshold's frames, and varying-cutoff C on common frames) are computed separately and are correctly labelled.

**5. Leave-one-out identity**
- `effective_cutoff = 0.5·(N−1)/N` is the correct cutoff for the identity v_i − v̄_all = ((N−1)/N)(v_i − v̄_other).
- Directions are unchanged, so only eligibility moves.

**6. Gaps, segments and truncated duration**
- `kinematics` groups by `(id, segment)` and splits blocks on `diff(frame) != 1`. It trims `w//2 + 1` samples from each end, unwraps heading within each block only, and never bridges a gap.
- The heading-jump support convolution has the correct length and covers ±half around each flagged pair.
- Matched-duration kinematics are recomputed on the truncated rows, so the prefix endpoint is trimmed. The supplied test expects 31 − 12 = 19 frames, which matches.

**7. Nonpositive-length handling**
- L is the median of positive lengths only.
- Curvature is NaN on affected rows in all neighborhoods. Position and heading are retained in primary metrics.
- The sensitivity analysis removes whole frames and recomputes kinematics, so the new gap is trimmed. The test's expected NaN span (frames 24–36 around frame 30) is consistent with this.
- For P, the sensitivity removes only the affected frame itself. That is appropriate because P is instantaneous. The recomputed jump detection no longer spans the removed frame.

**8. N=151 length scenario**
| Output | Treatment under L×1.15 |
|---|---|
| Speed, acceleration, spread, centroid speed, nearest-neighbor distance | Divided by 1.15 |
| Curvature × L | Multiplied by 1.15 |
| Spatial density | Multiplied by 1.15²; coordinates divided by 1.15 (algebra correct) |
| Turn rate | Unchanged (correct) |
| Threshold sweep, slip eligibility, reverse-motion diagnostics | Recomputed at the scaled L |

The limitation text covers the network and midline truncation.

**9. Streaming network** (`network_summary.summarize_network`)
- Bit packing uses `1 << (pair % 8)` at byte `pair // 8`, decoded with `unpackbits(bitorder='little')`. This is consistent.
- Each frame is padded to whole bytes, and the padding bits are sliced off.
- Duplicates are rejected both within and across batches.
- Reciprocity uses `A & Aᵀ`, which gives an edge-weighted count of directed edges.
- Zero-degree observers on covered frames are counted, via `bincount(minlength=n)` on the full degree matrix.
- The total edge count is checked against Parquet metadata and the packed sum.
- Primary and geometry-excluded counts are stored separately. The excluded degree histogram is the full histogram minus the excluded-frame histogram.

---

## Non-blocking findings

**N1. Threshold-panel identities should be asserted or annotated before the narrative.**
Because the sets are exactly nested (point 4), two outputs are fixed by construction:
- Baseline C on the 0.25 frame set is *identical* to baseline C on the 0.5 set. The plan says "overlaps", but the overlap is complete.
- `baseline_undefined_frames` at 1.0 must be 0.

So in `plot_thresholds` panel 4, the 0.25→0.5 segment is flat by construction. It should not be read as robustness.

Fix (no rerun needed): add these invariants to `validate_trial`, and add a caption note. Optionally add `common_frames == circulation n at 1.0`.

**N2. A common source snapshot across trials is not checked when plotting.**
- `run_comparison.validate_completed` does check that recorded source hashes match current files, but only on `--resume`.
- `plot_comparison` reads only `summary.json` and `collective.csv`.
- The plan requires all final trials to come from one common snapshot.

Fix: have `plot_comparison` (or a separate check) load each trial's `provenance.json` and require identical `source_hashes` for `compare_trial.py`, `metrics.py`, `network_summary.py` and the config. Record that in the manifest. If this check is not added, verify it by hand before results acceptance.

**N3. The circulation eligibility denominator mixes two causes.**
`circulation_eligible_frame_fraction` divides by all tracked frames. That includes frames where velocity is undefined because of edge trimming, not low relative motion. The plan asks for separate denominators.
- The effect is small: about 7 blocks × 12 trimmed frames in the smaller trials versus 1 × 12 at N=151, roughly 0.3%.
- It can be derived without a rerun: rows of `collective.csv` with finite `eligible_fraction` are the velocity-defined frames.
- Recommend reporting both fractions.

**N4. The affected-fish-only P on primary frames is identical by construction.**
`polarization_on_primary_valid_frames` equals primary P exactly, because all headings are valid on those frames. The plan already acknowledges this. The informative contrast is affected-fish-only P on the *added* frames (subset valid, primary masked), which is not summarized.

It can be derived without a rerun from `collective.csv` columns `polarization_valid_fish` and `heading_frame_valid`. Recommend adding it to the narrative tables.

**N5. The network matched-duration count is hard-coded.**
`summarize_network` uses 17999 and ignores the config `matched_frame_count`, while `compare_trial` reads `cfg.get('matched_frame_count', 17999)`.
- This is harmless in the current config, which omits the key, so both use 17999.
- It is a latent divergence that the `matched_frame_count=31` test does not catch, because that test runs without the network.
- Fix: pass the value through.

**N6. Scale scenario coverage is partial (optional).**
The window-sweep and leave-one-out circulation are not recomputed under L×1.15. The plan names only the threshold sweep, so this is an optional extension.

**N7. Minor disclosure items.**
- `body_length_px` quantiles include nonpositive values. This is fine if labelled as raw.
- `heading_axis_error` is not masked on nonpositive-length rows unless the pose is exactly collapsed (≤1e-8).
- Spatial occupancy has no nonpositive-length sensitivity; only nearest-neighbor distance does. The plan does not require one.
- A network frame with zero edges is indistinguishable from an uncovered frame. This is inherent to the edge-list format and consistent with the pilot; it is very unlikely at N≥10.

**N8. Figure 04 caption.**
The visibility and curvature panels include N=151. The caption says "different camera/length calibration" but should state explicitly that N=151 curvature and visibility are excluded from group-size claims, as the plan requires. This belongs to the narrative review.

  - the reciprocity value of 0.8

===== SOURCE src/shiners/compare_trial.py | SHA256 322382f5b180a5192c3e98c040c35569a27d4b907d611ed5b9251e31e6e93ff4 =====
"""Run the reviewed descriptive measurements on one trial, with bounded network IO.

One invocation/process per trial. This keeps each trial separate and releases its
memory on exit. A summary.json is written only after every requested stage passes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import gc
import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

from .metrics import kinematics, curvature, collective, spatial, heading_diagnostics

BASE_COLUMNS = ['frame', 'id', 'segment', 'time', 'X', 'Y', 'ANGLE', 'body_length']
IDENTITY_COLUMNS = ['group', 'sequence']
POSE_INDICES = [0, *range(6, 15), 20]
POSE_COLUMNS = [f'pose{axis}{i}' for axis in 'XY' for i in POSE_INDICES]
CORE_COLUMNS = BASE_COLUMNS + IDENTITY_COLUMNS + ['poseX0','poseY0','poseX20','poseY20']


def quant(values):
    a = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    a = a[np.isfinite(a)]
    return {'n': int(len(a)), **{str(q): float(np.quantile(a,q)) if len(a) else None
                               for q in [.05,.5,.95]}}


def file_hash(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with Path(path).open('rb') as f:
        for b in iter(lambda:f.read(1024*1024), b''): h.update(b)
    return h.hexdigest()


def atomic_json(path, value):
    # All values must be finite JSON numbers, or explicit null for undefined metrics.
    temporary = path.with_suffix(path.suffix+'.tmp')
    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(value,indent=2,allow_nan=False)+'\n')
    temporary.replace(path)


def validate_tracks(tracks):
    """Validate the projected fields actually used; do not claim unselected QC."""
    required = BASE_COLUMNS + IDENTITY_COLUMNS + POSE_COLUMNS
    missing = sorted(set(required)-set(tracks.columns))
    if missing: raise ValueError(f'Missing track columns: {missing}')
    if tracks.empty: raise ValueError('Empty tracks')
    for col in BASE_COLUMNS + POSE_COLUMNS:
        if not np.isfinite(tracks[col].to_numpy(dtype=float)).all():
            raise ValueError(f'Nonfinite track values: {col}')
    for col in ['frame','id','segment']:
        a = tracks[col].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        if (a != np.floor(a)).any(): raise ValueError(f'Noninteger track {col}')
    positive_length=tracks.body_length>0
    if not positive_length.any():raise ValueError('No positive body lengths for reference scale')
    bad_geometry=tracks.loc[~positive_length,['frame','id','segment','time','body_length']]
    bad_geometry_frames=sorted(int(f) for f in bad_geometry.frame.unique())
    for col in IDENTITY_COLUMNS:
        if tracks[col].isna().any() or tracks[col].nunique() != 1:
            raise ValueError(f'Expected one nonnull {col}')
    if tracks.duplicated(['frame','id']).any(): raise ValueError('Duplicate track keys')
    grouped = tracks.groupby('frame',sort=True)
    count = grouped.id.nunique()
    fish = int(tracks.id.nunique())
    if fish<2:raise ValueError('Social comparison requires at least two fish')
    if (count != fish).any(): raise ValueError('Incomplete fish set')
    if (grouped[['time','segment']].nunique() != 1).any().any():
        raise ValueError('Inconsistent time or segment inside a frame')
    frames = grouped[['time','segment']].first()
    if (np.diff(frames.time) <= 0).any(): raise ValueError('Nonmonotone frame times')
    if (np.diff(frames.segment) < 0).any(): raise ValueError('Nonmonotone segments')
    breaks = (frames.index.to_series().diff().fillna(1) != 1) | (frames.segment.diff().fillna(0) != 0)
    blocks = []
    for _, g in frames.groupby(breaks.cumsum()):
        delta = np.diff(g.time.to_numpy())
        if len(delta) and not np.allclose(delta,np.median(delta),rtol=1e-6,atol=1e-10):
            raise ValueError('Irregular timestamps inside continuous block')
        blocks.append({'segment':int(g.segment.iloc[0]),'first_frame':int(g.index.min()),
                       'last_frame':int(g.index.max()),'frames':int(len(g))})
    frame_steps = np.diff(frames.index.to_numpy())
    return {
        'track_rows':int(len(tracks)), 'fish':fish, 'frames':int(len(frames)),
        'frame_range':[int(frames.index.min()),int(frames.index.max())],
        'time_range_s':[float(frames.time.min()),float(frames.time.max())],
        'duration_s':float(frames.time.max()-frames.time.min()),
        'fps_from_track_timestamps':float(np.median(np.diff(frames.index)/np.diff(frames.time))) if len(frames)>1 else None,
        'segment_count':int(tracks.segment.nunique()), 'continuous_blocks':blocks,
        'missing_frames_inside_range':int(np.maximum(frame_steps-1,0).sum()),
        'nonpositive_length_rows':int(len(bad_geometry)),
        'nonpositive_length_frame_count':len(bad_geometry_frames),
        'nonpositive_length_frames':bad_geometry_frames,
        'nonpositive_length_observations':bad_geometry.to_dict('records'),
        'nonpositive_length_policy':'Reference length uses positive values only; curvature is explicitly undefined for nonpositive-length rows. Finite measured positions/headings remain in primary metrics. A separate full-frame exclusion sensitivity recomputes kinematics with gap guards.',
        'checked_columns':required,
        'qc_scope':'Projected measurement inputs only; unselected pose/eye columns are not audited.',
        'passed':['finite required numeric fields','unique track keys','complete fish set',
                  'positive reference length available; nonpositive values disclosed','single trial','consistent per-frame time/segment',
                  'monotone times/segments','regular within-block timestamps'],
    }


def collective_summary(c):
    eligible = np.isfinite(c.circulation.to_numpy())
    joint = eligible & np.isfinite(c.polarization.to_numpy())
    return {
        'tracked_frames':int(len(c)), 'circulation_valid_frames':int(eligible.sum()),
        'circulation_eligible_frame_fraction':float(eligible.mean()),
        'joint_valid_frames':int(joint.sum()), 'joint_eligible_frame_fraction':float(joint.mean()),
        'circulation':quant(c.circulation), 'circulation_median':quant(c.circulation)['0.5'],
        'signed_circulation':quant(c.signed_circulation),
        'polarization':quant(c.polarization),
        'polarization_valid_frames':int(np.isfinite(c.polarization).sum()),
        'polarization_eligible_frame_fraction':float(np.isfinite(c.polarization).mean()),
        'polarization_when_circulation_eligible':quant(c.loc[eligible,'polarization']),
        'polarization_when_circulation_ineligible_or_unknown':quant(c.loc[~eligible,'polarization']),
        'eligible_fish_fraction':quant(c.eligible_fraction),
        'iid_direction_reference':quant(c.iid_direction_reference),
    }


def heading_selection(k, c, min_fraction=.8):
    """Expose whole-frame versus affected-fish-only heading-mask selection."""
    n=int(k.id.nunique())
    units=pd.DataFrame({'frame':k.frame.to_numpy(), 'x':np.cos(k.ANGLE),
                        'y':np.sin(k.ANGLE), 'valid':k.heading_valid.astype(int)})
    units['valid_x']=units.x*units.valid;units['valid_y']=units.y*units.valid
    grouped=units.groupby('frame',sort=True)
    means=grouped[['x','y']].mean().reindex(c.frame)
    sums=grouped[['valid_x','valid_y','valid']].sum().reindex(c.frame)
    raw=np.hypot(means.x,means.y).to_numpy()
    n_valid=sums.valid.to_numpy(dtype=int)
    subset_valid=n_valid/n>=min_fraction
    subset=np.full(len(c),np.nan)
    subset[subset_valid]=np.hypot(sums.valid_x,sums.valid_y).to_numpy()[subset_valid]/n_valid[subset_valid]
    valid=np.isfinite(c.polarization.to_numpy())
    raw_median=quant(raw)['0.5'];masked_median=quant(c.polarization)['0.5']
    reference=np.full(len(c),np.nan);reference[valid]=np.sqrt(np.pi/(4*n))
    subset_reference=np.full(len(c),np.nan)
    subset_reference[subset_valid]=np.sqrt(np.pi/(4*n_valid[subset_valid]))
    frame_output=pd.DataFrame({'polarization_raw':raw,'polarization_valid_fish':subset,
        'heading_valid_fish_count':n_valid,'polarization_iid_reference':reference,
        'polarization_valid_fish_iid_reference':subset_reference})
    result={
        'raw_polarization':quant(raw), 'masked_polarization':quant(c.polarization),
        'raw_polarization_on_masked_frames':quant(raw[valid]),
        'raw_polarization_on_excluded_frames':quant(raw[~valid]),
        'raw_minus_masked_median':raw_median-masked_median if masked_median is not None else None,
        'polarization_valid_frames':int(valid.sum()),
        'polarization_eligible_frame_fraction':float(valid.mean()),
        'heading_jump_rows':int(k.heading_jump.sum()),
        'heading_jump_row_fraction':float(k.heading_jump.mean()),
        'heading_masked_rows':int((~k.heading_valid).sum()),
        'heading_masked_row_fraction':float((~k.heading_valid).mean()),
        'exclusion_reasons':{'any_fish_heading_jump_support':int((~valid).sum()),
                             'nonfinite_heading_input':0,'incomplete_fish_set':0},
        'affected_fish_only':{
            'minimum_heading_valid_fraction':float(min_fraction),
            'valid_fish_per_frame':quant(n_valid),
            'polarization':quant(subset),
            'valid_frames':int(subset_valid.sum()),'valid_frame_fraction':float(subset_valid.mean()),
            'polarization_on_primary_valid_frames':quant(subset[valid]),
            'primary_polarization_on_common_frames':quant(c.loc[valid,'polarization']),
            'common_frames':int(valid.sum()),
            'iid_reference':quant(subset_reference),
        },
        'polarization_iid_reference':quant(reference),
        'iid_reference_note':'sqrt(pi/(4*n)) approximates mean P for independent uniform headings. Illustrative only, not a calibrated null or subtraction/division correction; E[P squared]=1/n under that idealization.',
        'interpretation':'Raw uses all finite recorded headings; primary excludes an entire frame when any fish is heading-masked. Affected-fish-only sensitivity requires >=80% valid headings. Differences in medians describe selection and changing fish composition, not a correction.',
    }
    return frame_output,result


def common_cohort_summaries(tables, labels, label_name, require_polarization=True):
    """Same frame IDs eligible for every setting; fish composition may differ."""
    if not tables:raise ValueError('No settings')
    if len(tables)!=len(labels):raise ValueError('Setting labels mismatch')
    ref=tables[0].frame.to_numpy()
    if any(not np.array_equal(t.frame.to_numpy(),ref) for t in tables):
        raise ValueError('Sensitivity tables do not share frame ordering')
    masks=[np.isfinite(t.circulation) for t in tables]
    if require_polarization:masks=[m&np.isfinite(t.polarization) for m,t in zip(masks,tables)]
    mask=np.logical_and.reduce(masks)
    return {
        'common_frames':int(mask.sum()),'common_fraction':float(mask.mean()),
        'require_valid_polarization':require_polarization,
        'definition':'Same frames eligible for every setting; eligible fish may differ. For threshold sweeps this is a selected high-relative-motion subset, not representative of the trial.',
        'settings':[{label_name:float(label),'circulation':quant(t.loc[mask,'circulation']),
                     'signed_circulation':quant(t.loc[mask,'signed_circulation']),
                     'polarization':quant(t.loc[mask,'polarization'])}
                    for label,t in zip(labels,tables)],
    }


def threshold_frame_selection(baseline, tables, thresholds, baseline_threshold):
    """Keep C's calculation fixed while changing the eligible frame set."""
    result=[]
    for threshold,t in zip(thresholds,tables):
        frame_mask=np.isfinite(t.circulation.to_numpy())
        baseline_valid=np.isfinite(baseline.circulation.to_numpy())
        joint=frame_mask&baseline_valid
        result.append({'threshold_frame_set_bl_s':float(threshold),
                       'candidate_frames':int(frame_mask.sum()),
                       'baseline_valid_frames':int(joint.sum()),
                       'baseline_undefined_frames':int((frame_mask&~baseline_valid).sum()),
                       'baseline_circulation':quant(baseline.loc[joint,'circulation']),
                       'baseline_signed_circulation':quant(baseline.loc[joint,'signed_circulation'])})
    return {'baseline_threshold_bl_s':float(baseline_threshold),'settings':result,
            'interpretation':'Fixed baseline C sampled on each threshold-eligible frame set. Frames where baseline C is undefined are counted and excluded; especially relevant to the lower-threshold set.'}


def scaled_measurements(k, c, length, curve, low_speed):
    speed=np.hypot(k.vx,k.vy).to_numpy()/length
    slip=np.arctan2(np.sin(np.arctan2(k.vy,k.vx)-k.ANGLE),
                    np.cos(np.arctan2(k.vy,k.vx)-k.ANGLE))
    slip=np.where((speed>=low_speed)&k.heading_valid,slip,np.nan)
    return {'reference_length_px':float(length),'speed_bl_s':quant(speed),
            'acceleration_bl_s2':quant(np.hypot(k.ax,k.ay)/length),
            'turn_rate_rad_s':quant(k.turn_rate),'slip_rad':quant(slip),
            'curvature_times_L':quant(curve*length),'spread_bl':quant(c.spread_bl),
            'centroid_speed_bl_s':quant(c.centroid_speed_bl_s),
            **collective_summary(c)}


def histogram(values, edges, path):
    a=np.asarray(values,dtype=float);a=a[np.isfinite(a)]
    counts,_=np.histogram(a,bins=edges)
    pd.DataFrame({'left':edges[:-1],'right':edges[1:],'count':counts}).to_csv(path,index=False)
    return {'finite_n':int(len(a)), 'counted_n':int(counts.sum()),
            'underflow':int((a<edges[0]).sum()), 'overflow':int((a>edges[-1]).sum()),
            'range':[float(edges[0]),float(edges[-1])], 'bins':int(len(edges)-1)}


def validate_config(cfg):
    windows=cfg['smoothing_windows']; primary=cfg['primary_window']
    if primary not in windows or len(windows)!=len(set(windows)):
        raise ValueError('Primary window missing or duplicate windows')
    if any(type(w) is not int or w<5 or w%2!=1 for w in windows):
        raise ValueError('Invalid smoothing windows')
    neighborhoods=cfg['curvature_neighborhoods']
    if any(n not in [5,7,9] for n in neighborhoods) or cfg['primary_curvature_neighborhood'] not in neighborhoods:
        raise ValueError('Projection supports curvature neighborhoods 5,7,9')
    thresholds=cfg['low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s']
    if cfg['low_speed_bl_s'] not in thresholds or len(thresholds)!=len(set(thresholds)) or any(not np.isfinite(t) or t<=0 for t in thresholds):
        raise ValueError('Invalid direction thresholds')
    if not 0 < cfg['circulation_min_fraction'] <= 1:
        raise ValueError('Invalid circulation eligibility fraction')
    if not 1 <= cfg['polynomial_order'] < min(windows):
        raise ValueError('Invalid smoothing polynomial order')
    if type(cfg.get('matched_frame_count',17999)) is not int or cfg.get('matched_frame_count',17999)<1:
        raise ValueError('Invalid matched frame count')


def run(data, output, config, no_network=False):
    cfg=json.loads(config.read_text());validate_config(cfg)
    if output.exists() and any(output.iterdir()): raise ValueError('Output directory must be new or empty')
    provenance_file=data/'provenance.json'
    if not provenance_file.is_file(): raise ValueError('Missing fetch provenance')
    fetch_provenance=json.loads(provenance_file.read_text())
    output.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True); tables=output/'tables';tables.mkdir()
    path=data/'tracks.parquet'; parquet=pq.ParquetFile(path)
    available=parquet.schema_arrow.names
    requested=BASE_COLUMNS+IDENTITY_COLUMNS+POSE_COLUMNS
    if set(requested)-set(available): raise ValueError(f'Missing projected fields: {set(requested)-set(available)}')
    t=pd.read_parquet(path,columns=requested).sort_values(['frame','id']).reset_index(drop=True)
    quality=validate_tracks(t)
    group=str(t.group.iloc[0]); sequence=str(t.sequence.iloc[0]);trial=f'{group}/{sequence}'
    fish=quality['fish'];length=float(t.loc[t.body_length>0,'body_length'].median())
    bad_geometry_rows=(t.body_length<=0).to_numpy()
    bad_geometry_frames=quality['nonpositive_length_frames']
    print(f'{trial}: {len(t):,} rows, {fish} fish, measuring tracks',flush=True)
    curves={n:curvature(t,n) for n in cfg['curvature_neighborhoods']}
    for curve in curves.values():curve[bad_geometry_rows]=np.nan
    curve_common=np.logical_and.reduce([np.isfinite(x) for x in curves.values()])
    curvature_sensitivity=[{'neighborhood':n,**quant(v[curve_common]*length)} for n,v in curves.items()]
    core=t[CORE_COLUMNS].copy()
    primary=kinematics(core,cfg['primary_window'],cfg['polynomial_order'])
    speed=np.hypot(primary.vx,primary.vy).to_numpy()/length
    slip=np.arctan2(np.sin(np.arctan2(primary.vy,primary.vx)-primary.ANGLE),np.cos(np.arctan2(primary.vy,primary.vx)-primary.ANGLE))
    slip=np.where((speed>=cfg['low_speed_bl_s'])&primary.heading_valid,slip,np.nan)
    threshold_tables=[]; threshold_sensitivity=[]
    for threshold in cfg['low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s']:
        c=collective(primary,length,threshold,cfg['circulation_min_fraction'])
        c['eligible_fish_count']=np.rint(c.eligible_fraction*fish)
        c.to_csv(tables/f'collective-threshold-{threshold:g}.csv',index=False)
        threshold_tables.append(c)
        threshold_sensitivity.append({'threshold_bl_s':float(threshold),**collective_summary(c)})
    main_index=cfg['low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s'].index(cfg['low_speed_bl_s'])
    c=threshold_tables[main_index]
    c['heading_frame_valid']=np.isfinite(c.polarization)
    heading_frames,heading_sensitivity=heading_selection(primary,c,cfg['circulation_min_fraction'])
    for column in heading_frames:c[column]=heading_frames[column].to_numpy()
    c.to_csv(output/'collective.csv',index=False)
    threshold_common=common_cohort_summaries(threshold_tables,cfg['low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s'],'threshold_bl_s')
    threshold_c_common=common_cohort_summaries(threshold_tables,cfg['low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s'],'threshold_bl_s',False)
    frame_selection=threshold_frame_selection(c,threshold_tables,cfg['low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s'],cfg['low_speed_bl_s'])
    # Independent settings are processed sequentially; retain only speed arrays and frame summaries.
    speeds={cfg['primary_window']:speed}; window_tables={cfg['primary_window']:c}
    for window in cfg['smoothing_windows']:
        if window==cfg['primary_window']:continue
        motion=kinematics(core,window,cfg['polynomial_order'])
        speeds[window]=np.hypot(motion.vx,motion.vy).to_numpy()/length
        window_tables[window]=collective(motion,length,cfg['low_speed_bl_s'],cfg['circulation_min_fraction'])
        del motion;gc.collect()
    speed_common=np.logical_and.reduce([np.isfinite(s) for s in speeds.values()])
    speed_sensitivity=[{'window':w,**quant(speeds[w][speed_common])} for w in cfg['smoothing_windows']]
    window_sensitivity=[{'window':w,**collective_summary(window_tables[w])} for w in cfg['smoothing_windows']]
    window_common=common_cohort_summaries([window_tables[w] for w in cfg['smoothing_windows']],cfg['smoothing_windows'],'window')
    effective_cutoff=cfg['low_speed_bl_s']*(fish-1)/fish
    loo=collective(primary,length,effective_cutoff,cfg['circulation_min_fraction'])
    loo_summary={'effective_all_mean_cutoff_bl_s':effective_cutoff,
                 'other_fish_cutoff_bl_s':cfg['low_speed_bl_s'],
                 'interpretation':'Speed-threshold equivalent to subtracting the other-fish mean; directions and primary measurements unchanged. The tiny radius eligibility tolerance is retained.',
                 **collective_summary(loo)}
    scale_sensitivity=None
    if fish==151:
        scaled_tables=[collective(primary,length*1.15,threshold,cfg['circulation_min_fraction'])
                       for threshold in cfg['low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s']]
        scaled=scaled_tables[main_index]
        scaled.to_csv(tables/'collective-Lx1p15.csv',index=False)
        scale_sensitivity={'scenario':'Illustrative reference length increased by 15%; not a correction or new physical calibration.',
                           **scaled_measurements(primary,scaled,length*1.15,
                               curves[cfg['primary_curvature_neighborhood']],cfg['low_speed_bl_s']),
                           'speed_sensitivity':[{'window':w,**quant(speeds[w][speed_common]/1.15)} for w in cfg['smoothing_windows']],
                           'curvature_sensitivity':[{'neighborhood':n,**quant(v[curve_common]*length*1.15)} for n,v in curves.items()],
                           'heading_diagnostics':heading_diagnostics(primary,length*1.15,cfg['low_speed_bl_s']),
                           'threshold_sensitivity':[{'threshold_bl_s':float(threshold),**collective_summary(table)}
                               for threshold,table in zip(cfg['low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s'],scaled_tables)],
                           'threshold_common_eligible':common_cohort_summaries(scaled_tables,cfg['low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s'],'threshold_bl_s'),
                           'threshold_circulation_common_eligible':common_cohort_summaries(scaled_tables,cfg['low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s'],'threshold_bl_s',False),
                           'threshold_frame_selection':threshold_frame_selection(scaled,scaled_tables,cfg['low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s'],cfg['low_speed_bl_s']),
                           'limitation':'Changing L cannot repair an anatomically truncated or otherwise biased midline, nor rerender the ray-cast visual network. N=151 curvature and network metrics are not comparable for a size-trend claim.'}
    target_frames=int(cfg.get('matched_frame_count',17999))
    cutoff_frames=c.frame.iloc[:target_frames].to_numpy()
    matched_rows=core.frame.isin(cutoff_frames).to_numpy()
    matched=primary if len(cutoff_frames)==len(c) else kinematics(core.loc[matched_rows],cfg['primary_window'],cfg['polynomial_order'])
    matched_c=collective(matched,length,cfg['low_speed_bl_s'],cfg['circulation_min_fraction'])
    matched_h,matched_heading=heading_selection(matched,matched_c,cfg['circulation_min_fraction'])
    for column in matched_h:matched_c[column]=matched_h[column].to_numpy()
    matched_c.to_csv(tables/'collective-matched-duration.csv',index=False)
    matched_summary={'target_frame_count':target_frames,'frame_count':int(len(cutoff_frames)),
                     'frame_start':int(cutoff_frames[0]),'frame_end':int(cutoff_frames[-1]),
                     'duration_s':float(matched_c.time.max()-matched_c.time.min()),
                     **scaled_measurements(matched,matched_c,length,
                         curves[cfg['primary_curvature_neighborhood']][matched_rows],cfg['low_speed_bl_s']),
                     'heading_selection_sensitivity':matched_heading,
                     'definition':'First min(target, available) sorted observed frames; kinematics recomputed with the truncated endpoint, retaining original segment/gap boundaries.'}
    del matched;gc.collect()
    geometry_rows=~core.frame.isin(bad_geometry_frames).to_numpy()
    if bad_geometry_frames:
        if not geometry_rows.any():raise ValueError('No complete frames remain for bad-geometry sensitivity')
        geometry_motion=kinematics(core.loc[geometry_rows],cfg['primary_window'],cfg['polynomial_order'])
        geometry_c=collective(geometry_motion,length,cfg['low_speed_bl_s'],cfg['circulation_min_fraction'])
        geometry_h,geometry_heading=heading_selection(geometry_motion,geometry_c,cfg['circulation_min_fraction'])
        for column in geometry_h:geometry_c[column]=geometry_h[column].to_numpy()
    else:
        geometry_motion=primary;geometry_c=c;geometry_heading=heading_sensitivity
    geometry_summary={
        'excluded_frames':bad_geometry_frames,'excluded_frame_count':len(bad_geometry_frames),
        'source_frame_count':int(len(c)), 'retained_frame_count':int(len(geometry_c)),
        'excluded_fish_observations':int((~geometry_rows).sum()),
        **scaled_measurements(geometry_motion,geometry_c,length,
            curves[cfg['primary_curvature_neighborhood']][geometry_rows],cfg['low_speed_bl_s']),
        'heading_selection_sensitivity':geometry_heading,
        'circulation_valid_frame_fraction_of_source':float(np.isfinite(geometry_c.circulation).sum()/len(c)),
        'polarization_valid_frame_fraction_of_source':float(np.isfinite(geometry_c.polarization).sum()/len(c)),
        'definition':'Remove the complete frame whenever any fish has nonpositive body length, then recompute kinematics so smoothing never bridges the resulting gap. This is a sensitivity, not a claim that all retained finite primary positions/headings are correct. Own-set coverage uses retained frames; source-frame coverage is also recorded.',
    }
    common=c[['frame','polarization','circulation']].merge(
        geometry_c[['frame','polarization','circulation']],on='frame',suffixes=('_primary','_sensitivity'))
    geometry_summary['common_frame_comparison']={}
    for metric in ['polarization','circulation']:
        mask=np.isfinite(common[f'{metric}_primary'])&np.isfinite(common[f'{metric}_sensitivity'])
        geometry_summary['common_frame_comparison'][metric]={
            'frames':int(mask.sum()),'primary':quant(common.loc[mask,f'{metric}_primary']),
            'sensitivity':quant(common.loc[mask,f'{metric}_sensitivity'])}
    if bad_geometry_frames:
        geometry_export=c[['frame','time','segment']].merge(geometry_c.drop(columns=['time','segment']),on='frame',how='left')
        geometry_export['geometry_frame_retained']=~geometry_export.frame.isin(bad_geometry_frames)
        geometry_export.to_csv(tables/'collective-nonpositive-length-exclusion.csv',index=False)
    del geometry_motion;gc.collect()
    diagnostics=heading_diagnostics(primary,length,cfg['low_speed_bl_s'])
    space=spatial(core,length,cfg['spatial_extent_bl'],cfg['spatial_bins'])
    histograms={}
    for name,values,edges in [
        ('speed',speed,np.linspace(0,12,121)),
        ('turn',primary.turn_rate,np.linspace(-20,20,161)),
        ('curvature',curves[cfg['primary_curvature_neighborhood']]*length,np.linspace(-5,5,161)),
        ('nearest',space['nearest'].distance_bl,np.linspace(0,20,161)),
        ('polarization',c.polarization,np.linspace(0,1,51)),
        ('circulation',c.circulation,np.linspace(0,1,51)),
    ]:
        histograms[name]=histogram(values,edges,tables/f'{name}-histogram.csv')
    edges=space['bin_edges'];centers=(edges[1:]+edges[:-1])/2
    xx,yy=np.meshgrid(centers,centers,indexing='ij')
    spatial_table=pd.DataFrame({'forward_bl':xx.ravel(),'right_bl':yy.ravel(),'count':space['histogram'].ravel(),
                  'density_per_focal_per_bl2':space['density'].ravel()})
    spatial_table.to_csv(tables/'spatial-map.csv',index=False)
    matched_summary['nearest_neighbor_bl']=quant(space['nearest'].loc[space['nearest'].frame.isin(cutoff_frames),'distance_bl'])
    geometry_summary['nearest_neighbor_bl']=quant(space['nearest'].loc[~space['nearest'].frame.isin(bad_geometry_frames),'distance_bl'])
    if scale_sensitivity is not None:
        scale_sensitivity['nearest_neighbor_bl']=quant(space['nearest'].distance_bl/1.15)
        scaled_spatial=spatial_table.copy()
        scaled_spatial[['forward_bl','right_bl']]/=1.15
        scaled_spatial['density_per_focal_per_bl2']*=1.15**2
        scaled_spatial.to_csv(tables/'spatial-map-Lx1p15.csv',index=False)
        scale_sensitivity['spatial_map']={'density_multiplier':1.15**2,
            'coordinate_divisor':1.15,'extent_bl':cfg['spatial_extent_bl']/1.15,
            'normalization':'Original physical cells/pairs transformed to the new length units; coordinates divide by 1.15 and density multiplies by 1.15 squared. Not rebinned into a new fixed +/-10 BL crop.'}
    nearest_quant=quant(space['nearest'].distance_bl)
    spatial_summary={'focal_count':int(space['focal_count']),
                     'shown_pair_fraction':float(space['shown_pair_fraction']),
                     'extent_bl':cfg['spatial_extent_bl'],'bins':cfg['spatial_bins'],
                     'normalization':'Counts divided by all focal observations and bin area; visible map need not integrate to one.'}
    del space,core;gc.collect()
    summary={
        'trial':trial,'group':group,'sequence':sequence,'fish':fish,'quality':quality,
        'scope':'All valid observations of this trial; descriptive estimates, not independent samples or causal effects.',
        'length_scale_px':length,'body_length_px':quant(t.body_length),'speed_bl_s':quant(speed),
        'acceleration_bl_s2':quant(np.hypot(primary.ax,primary.ay)/length),
        'turn_rate_rad_s':quant(primary.turn_rate),'slip_rad':quant(slip),
        'curvature_times_L':quant(curves[cfg['primary_curvature_neighborhood']]*length),
        'curvature_sensitivity':curvature_sensitivity,'speed_sensitivity':speed_sensitivity,
        'polarization':quant(c.polarization),'circulation':quant(c.circulation),
        'signed_circulation':quant(c.signed_circulation),'spread_bl':quant(c.spread_bl),
        'centroid_speed_bl_s':quant(c.centroid_speed_bl_s),'nearest_neighbor_bl':nearest_quant,
        'threshold_sensitivity':threshold_sensitivity,'threshold_common_eligible':threshold_common,
        'threshold_circulation_common_eligible':threshold_c_common,
        'threshold_frame_selection':frame_selection,
        'window_sensitivity':window_sensitivity,'window_common_eligible':window_common,
        'leave_one_out_threshold_sensitivity':loo_summary,'scale_sensitivity_151':scale_sensitivity,
