===== SOURCE reports/comparison/README.md | SHA256 112c49e5d0a13e72d0c39b8c1a4ca2c44688634a1f0a64d8f05f252d0f7dbd96 =====
# Ten-trial golden-shiner comparison

**The clearest repeated pattern is lower global heading alignment across the 10-, 30- and 70-fish recordings. Circulation is much more variable and strongly dependent on which frames pass the relative-speed cutoff.** The single 151-fish recording does not extend a simple monotone pattern: its median alignment and circulation lie within the ranges of the 70-fish trials.

This extends the same five descriptive chapters to all ten trials: 10,827,539 fish-frame track rows, 266,688,111 directed visual-network rows, and 239,246 observed group frames. These are measurement counts, not independent experimental replicates. There are three trials at each of N=10, 30, 70 and one at N=151. No force, leadership, response-propagation or causal model has been fitted.

## 1. Alignment and circulation: what repeats

![Alignment and circulation across all ten trials](figures/01-alignment-circulation.png)

Each marker is one trial's median. Whiskers show that trial's 5th–95th percentiles over eligible frames, **not confidence intervals**. The statement that group medians separate concerns the markers, not the overlapping whiskers. P is the length of the mean heading vector, from 0 to 1; it is not the percentage of fish aligned. C is coherence of tangential movement around the moving group center after subtracting mean velocity. It is not angular speed or a validated milling classifier.

| Fish | Trial | Median P | P coverage | Median C | C coverage |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 | 0066 | 0.894 | 99.9% | 0.383 | 46.6% |
| 10 | 0105 | 0.919 | 99.8% | 0.287 | 37.3% |
| 10 | 0126 | 0.943 | 100.0% | 0.301 | 72.5% |
| 30 | 0084 | 0.827 | 99.1% | 0.268 | 44.1% |
| 30 | 0115 | 0.809 | 99.8% | 0.344 | 45.7% |
| 30 | 0120 | 0.811 | 99.6% | 0.397 | 55.9% |
| 70 | 0103 | 0.694 | 99.0% | 0.379 | 36.5% |
| 70 | 0107 | 0.509 | 99.3% | 0.781 | 10.6% |
| 70 | 0124 | 0.510 | 99.2% | 0.681 | 5.9% |
| 151 | 150-fish | 0.641 | 98.0% | 0.484 | 87.1% |

Coverage uses all observed group frames as its denominator. P excludes a frame when any fish's heading lies in the temporal support of a flagged large heading jump. C requires valid velocities and at least 80% of fish above 0.5 reference body lengths/s in centroid-relative speed. An undefined C is not zero circulation. The [trial table](tables/trials.csv) also gives velocity-defined frame counts and C coverage among those frames, separating boundary trimming from the relative-motion requirement.

Across the three trials in each smaller group, median P ranges are **0.894–0.943 (N=10), 0.809–0.827 (N=30), and 0.509–0.694 (N=70)**. Every 10-fish median exceeds every 30-fish median, and every 30-fish median exceeds every 70-fish median. This meets the comparison's predeclared, descriptive nonoverlap criterion. It survives raw-heading versus affected-fish-only summaries, smoothing windows 7/11/15, exclusion of invalid-length frames, and restriction to the first 17,999 observed frames. With matched duration, the ranges are 0.882–0.945,0.794–0.866, and 0.455–0.701.

This describes these recordings; it does not show that adding fish causes weaker social alignment. Global P can fall when different parts of a school move in different directions, including organized rotation. It does not measure local alignment or interaction strength. P also depends on N even for random headings. The dotted approximate-mean reference sqrt(pi/(4N)) is illustrative, not a calibrated null, expected median, significance threshold or correction. No experimental control or dependent-fish null was fitted.

Median C ranges are **0.287–0.383,0.268–0.397, and 0.379–0.781** at N=10, 30, 70. Adjacent ranges overlap, so C does not meet the strict monotone criterion. The two high-C 70-fish trials,0107 and 0124, have only 10.6% and 5.9% primary coverage. Calling them continuously circling schools, or treating those percentages as milling time, would exceed the evidence.

## 2. Why the circulation cutoff matters

![Circulation eligibility and threshold sensitivities](figures/02-circulation-thresholds.png)

The upper-left panel shows how much data remains; upper-right shows each cutoff's median on its own selected frames. Lower-left holds frames fixed at those qualifying at all three cutoffs, which is exactly the 1.0-eligible, high-relative-motion subset. Fish contributing within those frames can still differ. Lower-right keeps the 0.5-cutoff C calculation fixed and changes its overlapping frame set. Its 0.25-to 0.5 flat segment is identical by construction, not evidence of robustness. Missing C markers mean undefined summaries, never zero.

Trial 70-fish/0107 illustrates the main selection issue. At 0.25 BL/s, C is measurable in 74.6% of frames and its median is 0.441. At 0.5, coverage falls to 10.6% and the median becomes 0.781. At 1.0 there are no eligible frames; the prespecified three-way intersection is therefore empty. Trial 0124 also has no 1.0-eligible frames.

An explicitly exploratory [pairwise comparison](tables/threshold-pairs.csv) uses the 2,598 frames shared by 0.25 and 0.5 in 0107. On those same frames, the lower-cutoff median is already 0.742, compared with 0.781 at the higher cutoff. Most of the 0.441-to 0.781 difference therefore reflects selection of different moments; a smaller part reflects which fish contribute within those moments. These are descriptive differences between medians, not causal effects or independent-frame tests. All 30 threshold pairs, including undefined comparisons, are retained with [provenance](tables/threshold-pairs-manifest.json).

The focal fish's contribution to school-average velocity was also checked. Subtracting the other-fish mean rescales relative velocity by N/(N−1), leaving directions unchanged. Applying the equivalent threshold increases C coverage by 0.29–10.45 percentage points across these trials; the largest absolute change in median C is 0.0246. It does not rescue a monotone group-size ordering. This is a cutoff sensitivity, not a correction to the valid moving-centroid description.

## 3. Movement, posture, school size, spacing and visual access

![Other descriptive chapters across trials](figures/04-other-chapters.png)

The table gives the range of the three trial estimates in each smaller group. Movement, spread and spacing use trial medians; visibility uses each trial's mean fraction/degree and its pooled reciprocal-edge fraction.

| Measurement | N=10 | N=30 | N=70 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Median speed, BL/s |1.376–2.259|1.378–1.593|0.713–1.160|
| Median RMS radius, BL |2.202–2.970|3.707–5.069|4.979–5.751|
| Median nearest-neighbor spacing, BL |1.114–1.467|0.968–1.274|0.876–1.063|
| Mean visible neighbors |6.555–6.929|14.777–16.979|21.565–25.321|
| Mean fraction of other fish visible |72.83–76.99%|50.95–58.55%|31.25–36.70%|
| Reciprocal-edge fraction |82.73–85.08%|76.17–77.57%|69.83–72.25%|

**Movement:** all three 70-fish trials have lower median swimming speed than every 10- or 30-fish trial. This survives matching duration. The 10- and 30-fish ranges overlap, so there is no strict three-group monotone speed ordering. Trial 0084 is duration-sensitive: median speed changes from 1.378 to 1.703 BL/s in the first 17,999 frames, an increase of 23.6%. Recorded speed differences should not be treated as context-free properties of group size.

**Posture:** signed curvature and turn-rate distributions include both signs and overlap between groups. Near-zero signed medians can result from cancellation and do not demonstrate little turning or bending. The curvature estimate comes from a local cubic fit around the midpoint of the recorded midline; it is not a direct force measurement. No robust monotone claim about bending intensity is made.

**School organization and spatial relationships:** larger groups occupy a broader whole-school footprint while typical nearest-neighbor distances remain around one reference body length. The group center is the arithmetic mean of smoothed fish positions; RMS radius is the square root of mean squared distance from that center. Full-duration N=30 and 70 spread ranges overlap slightly; their separation appears after matching duration, so a strict spread ordering is not robust to the time window. Nearest spacing overlaps between adjacent group sizes. A larger total school footprint does not by itself establish wider local spacing.

**Visual access:** the number of geometrically visible neighbors rises across 10→30→70, while the fraction of the group visible and reciprocal-edge fraction fall. The adjacent ranges do not overlap, and these orderings survive matched duration and removal of invalid-length frames. These are properties of the supplied ray-cast geometry. They do not establish attention, information use, response strength or influence. An observed edge means observer id1 sees id2; reciprocity is the fraction of directed edges with a reverse edge, pooled over covered frames.

## 4. The 151-fish recording is a separate comparison

Its median P is 0.641 and C is 0.484, with C defined in 87.1% of observed frames. Both medians lie within the 70-fish ranges. Its median speed is 1.861 BL/s, above the 70-fish range, so the lower speed observed at 70 does not continue in this recording.

It contains 17,999 frames in one segment with no internal missing frames, versus seven segments and six missing join frames in each smaller trial. It uses a different camera, and the source reports visible bodies about 15% longer than the stored reference length. With the illustrative L×1.15 scenario, speed becomes 1.618 BL/s, RMS radius changes from 8.927 to 7.763 BL, and nearest spacing from 0.985 to 0.857 BL. Reapplying the circulation cutoff reduces coverage from 87.1% to 77.4% and changes median C from 0.484 to 0.507. P is unchanged by this length rescaling.

This scenario is not a calibrated correction: it cannot repair anatomical midline differences or regenerate the visual network from corrected outlines. **The 151-fish curvature and visibility measurements are excluded from group-size claims.** One recording under different conditions cannot establish a group-size effect. Source timing is 29.97 fps and time=frame/29.97; we have not independently verified this video's timing or camera orientation. Signed circulation is not compared across cameras.

## 5. Quality checks, time series and what remains uncertain

![Alignment and circulation time series for all ten trials](figures/03-collective-timelines.png)

Time series retain every observed group frame and break at segment boundaries, gaps and undefined measurements. They show variation during each recording; no persistence scale, transition rate or state-duration estimate is claimed.

The measured input columns passed finite-value, complete-fish-set, unique-key and within-block timing checks. Every network row was processed and checked, including duplicate edges, endpoints, ray/angular consistency and distances. Every observed track frame had a represented network, so covered-frame degree summaries include zero-degree fish. Entirely missing edge-list frames would remain unknown. This audits the selected measurement columns and supplied geometry; it does not validate unused pose columns or prove that tracking identities and headings are biologically correct.

There are 22 nonpositive-length fish observations across 14 trial-frames, with collapsed posture geometry. Reference L uses positive lengths only and curvature is undefined on those rows. Primary finite positions/headings and the supplied network remain recorded measurements. A separate sensitivity removes affected frames, recomputes motion with gap guards, and excludes those frames from network summaries. The largest changes in median P and C are only 0.000110 and 0.0000731, respectively. This demonstrates robustness of these summaries to those particular flagged frames, not that all tracking errors have been eliminated.

Primary P coverage is 98.0–99.95%. Dropping only affected fish instead of entire heading-flagged frames changes median P by at most 0.00144 and preserves the 10→30→70 ordering. Added-frame P summaries and all changing denominators are retained in the compact tables. Heading anomalies remain candidates for video inspection; they are not established head-tail flips. No additional videos were inspected for this comparison; the original pilot retains its earlier selected overlays.

**Computational QA:**131 tests and 8 subtests pass. The [validator](validation.json) verifies all recorded input/source/output hashes and identical analysis source/config across the ten runs. All ten primary quantile dictionaries and network summaries for 0066 exactly reproduce the pilot. Fifty independently recalculated sampled P values differ by at most 2.23×10⁻¹⁶. This is coordinator-run QA, not an independent rerun of every metric.

**Review status:** Claude Opus 5.5 independently passed the [implementation snapshot](../../docs/workflow/reviews/comparison-implementation/review.md); its [notes were dispositioned](../../docs/workflow/reviews/comparison-implementation/adjudication.md). Final numerical-results/narrative review is pending. Claude receives explicit source/results text without tools: it does not execute the data pipeline or inspect rendered images. The coordinator inspected the plots. Independent computational reproduction remains a separate unfinished gate.

## A defensible Monday summary

“We extended the descriptive analysis to all ten recordings. Across the three trials at each of 10,30 and 70 fish, larger groups had lower whole-school heading alignment; that ordering survived our heading filters, smoothing, time-window and flagged-geometry checks. Circulation varied substantially between trials and depended strongly on the relative-speed cutoff, so we cannot yet label milling states or infer how long they lasted. Typical local spacing stayed around one body length, while geometric visual access covered a smaller fraction of larger groups. The 151-fish trial is informative but has a different camera and only one replicate. These results identify behavior to investigate; they do not yet identify social forces, leadership or causation.”

## Files and reproduction

[Trial estimates and denominators](tables/trials.csv) · [Threshold summaries](tables/thresholds.csv) · [All sensitivity values](tables/sensitivity.csv) · [Metric quantiles](tables/metrics.csv) · [Plot inputs](plot-manifest.json) · [Run log](run-log.txt) · [Download verification](download-log.txt).

Per-trial summaries, configs, histogram tables and provenance are in `trials/<trial>/`. Large frame-level CSVs remain local ignored caches; scripts regenerate them. Raw tracks/networks stay in ignored `data/trials/`, outside Git. PNG figures have matching editable-text SVGs. Use the [repository reproduction commands](../../README.md#compare-all-ten-trials) with a new output directory. Measurement definitions and predeclared comparison criteria are in [comparison methods](../../docs/comparison-methods.md) and [pilot methods](../../docs/methods.md).

The next scientific work is to inspect selected high-C intervals against video, compare local versus global alignment, and then test predictive response models with explicit nulls and held-out trials. Independent computational reproduction is still required before treating this as a fully independently verified release. No commit, push or publication was requested or performed.

===== SOURCE tests/test_claude_review.py | SHA256 e5a46c92dcac9c59a23694b2abf8e7fd841dc8f21641b48e873e11ace8163485 =====
"""Offline tests: no Claude service, credentials, or model calls are used."""

import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch


SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts" / "claude_review.py"
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("claude_review", SCRIPT)
review = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(review)


class ReviewTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name).resolve()
        (self.root / "prompt.md").write_text("Review the definition; do not execute code.\n")
        (self.root / "method.md").write_text("Polarization is the norm of the mean unit heading.\n")

    def call(self, **kwargs):
        return review.run_review("prompt.md", ["method.md"], "reviews/run1", root=self.root, **kwargs)

    def mocked_run(self, response, code=0):
        def run(command, **kwargs):
            if command[0] == "git":
                text = "abc123\n" if command[1] == "rev-parse" else "?? method.md\n"
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, 0, text, "")
            return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, code, response, "diagnostic\n")
        return run

    def status(self):
        return json.loads((self.root / "reviews/run1/status.json").read_text())

    def test_success_saves_exact_snapshot_and_actual_model_without_acceptance(self):
        raw = json.dumps({"is_error": False, "result": "Verdict: CHANGES_REQUESTED", "modelUsage": {"actual-model": {}}, "session_id": "test-session"})
        with patch.object(review.subprocess, "run", side_effect=self.mocked_run(raw)) as run:
            path = self.call(model="chosen-model")
        command = run.call_args.args[0]
        self.assertEqual(command[command.index("--model") + 1], "chosen-model")
        self.assertEqual(command[command.index("--tools") + 1], "")
        self.assertNotIn("--fallback-model", command)
        self.assertIn("--safe-mode", command)
        packet = run.call_args.kwargs["input"]
        out = path.parent
        self.assertEqual((out / "snapshot.txt").read_text(), packet)
        self.assertEqual((out / "response.json").read_text(), raw)
        manifest = json.loads((out / "manifest.json").read_text())
        self.assertEqual(manifest["packet_sha256"], review.sha256(packet.encode()))
        self.assertTrue(manifest["git"]["dirty"])
        self.assertEqual(self.status()["reported_models"], ["actual-model"])
        self.assertEqual(self.status()["state"], "response_received")
        self.assertEqual(self.status()["scientific_acceptance"], "not_adjudicated")

    def test_default_does_not_select_or_replace_model(self):
        with patch.object(review.subprocess, "run", side_effect=self.mocked_run('{"result":"Review text"}')) as run:
            self.call()
        self.assertNotIn("--model", run.call_args.args[0])

    def test_error_responses_are_recorded_and_rejected(self):
        cases = [('{"is_error":true,"result":"no access"}', 0),
                 ('{"result":""}', 0), ('{"result":42}', 0),
                 ('not json', 0), ('[]', 0), ('denied', 1)]
        for number, (response, code) in enumerate(cases):
            with self.subTest(response=response):
                out = f"reviews/error{number}"
                with patch.object(review.subprocess, "run", side_effect=self.mocked_run(response, code)):
                    with self.assertRaises(review.ReviewError):
                        review.run_review("prompt.md", ["method.md"], out, root=self.root)
                status = json.loads((self.root / out / "status.json").read_text())
                self.assertEqual(status["state"], "failed")
                self.assertFalse((self.root / out / "review.md").exists())
                self.assertEqual((self.root / out / "response.json").read_text(), response)

    def test_timeout_preserves_partial_output(self):
        def run(command, **kwargs):
            if command[0] == "git":
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, 0, "", "")
            raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(command, 5, output=b"partial", stderr=b"slow")
        with patch.object(review.subprocess, "run", side_effect=run):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(review.ReviewError, "Timed out"):
                self.call(timeout=5)
        self.assertEqual(self.status()["state"], "failed")
        self.assertEqual((self.root / "reviews/run1/response.json").read_text(), "partial")

    def test_missing_executable_records_failure(self):
        def run(command, **kwargs):
            if command[0] == "git":
                return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, 0, "", "")
            raise FileNotFoundError("claude")
        with patch.object(review.subprocess, "run", side_effect=run):
            with self.assertRaises(review.ReviewError):
                self.call()
        self.assertEqual(self.status()["state"], "failed")

    def test_unsafe_input_and_output_paths_are_rejected(self):
        for name in [".env", ".env.local", "id_rsa", "secret.pem"]:
            (self.root / name).write_text("example secret")
            with self.assertRaises(review.ReviewError):
                review.read_source(name, self.root)
        with self.assertRaises(review.ReviewError):
            review.repository_path("../outside.md", self.root)
        (self.root / "alias.md").symlink_to(self.root / "method.md")
        with self.assertRaises(review.ReviewError):
            review.read_source("alias.md", self.root)
        (self.root / "outalias").symlink_to(self.root, target_is_directory=True)
        with self.assertRaises(review.ReviewError):
            review.repository_path("outalias/review", self.root)

    def test_binary_oversized_and_duplicate_inputs_rejected(self):
        (self.root / "binary.md").write_bytes(b"\xff\x00")
        with self.assertRaises(review.ReviewError):
            review.read_source("binary.md", self.root)
        with patch.object(review, "MAX_FILE_BYTES", 1):
            with self.assertRaises(review.ReviewError):
                review.read_source("method.md", self.root)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(review.ReviewError, "Duplicate"):
            review.build_packet("prompt.md", ["method.md", "method.md"], self.root)

    def test_prior_output_is_never_overwritten(self):
        with patch.object(review.subprocess, "run", side_effect=self.mocked_run('{"result":"first"}')):
            path = self.call()
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(review.ReviewError, "never overwritten"):
                self.call()
        self.assertEqual(path.read_text(), "first\n")

    def test_invalid_timeout_and_blank_model(self):
        for timeout in [0, -1, float("nan"), float("inf")]:
            with self.assertRaises(review.ReviewError):
                self.call(timeout=timeout)
        with self.assertRaises(review.ReviewError):
            self.call(model=" ")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

===== SOURCE tests/test_compare_threshold_pairs.py | SHA256 fba4bd6a73eed287a46cea57c87b48f165309225a2703e7c7cc81103100e1746 =====
"""Pairwise follow-up distinguishes selected time frames from fish composition."""
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('compare_threshold_pairs',Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]/'scripts/compare_threshold_pairs.py')
pairs=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec);spec.loader.exec_module(pairs)


def tables():
    low=pd.DataFrame({'frame':[1,2,4,5],'time':[.1,.2,.4,.5],'segment':[0,0,1,1],
                      'polarization':[.2,.5,np.nan,.9],'circulation':[.1,.2,.3,.4]})
    medium=low.copy();medium['circulation']=[np.nan,np.nan,.5,.9]
    high=low.copy();high['circulation']=np.nan
    return {.25:low,.5:medium,1.:high}


def test_pair_survives_empty_three_way_intersection_and_decomposes_medians():
    result=pairs.pair_rows('10-fish/example',10,tables())
    assert len(result)==3
    informative=result[0]
    assert informative['common_frames']==2
    assert informative['common_fraction']==.5
    assert informative['common_low_c_median']==pytest.approx(.35)
    assert informative['common_high_c_median']==pytest.approx(.7)
    assert informative['common_low_p_n']==1
    assert informative['common_low_p_median']==.9
    assert informative['low_own_c_median']==.25
    assert informative['low_c_on_high_frames_median']==pytest.approx(.35)
    assert informative['frame_selection_median_shift']==pytest.approx(.1)
    assert informative['fish_composition_median_shift']==pytest.approx(.35)
    assert informative['total_own_median_shift']==pytest.approx(.45)
    for empty in result[1:]:
        assert empty['common_frames']==0
        assert empty['common_high_c_median'] is None
        assert empty['frame_selection_median_shift'] is None
        assert empty['common_low_p_n']==0


@pytest.mark.parametrize('fault,error',[
    ('order','differ in frame'),('nonmonotone','higher-threshold eligibility'),
    ('heading','polarization changed'),('infinite','invalid circulation'),
])
def test_invalid_cross_threshold_handoffs_are_rejected(fault,error):
    data=tables()
    if fault=='order':data[.5]=data[.5].iloc[::-1]
    if fault=='nonmonotone':
        data[.25].loc[0,'circulation']=np.nan
        data[.5].loc[0,'circulation']=.4
    if fault=='heading':data[.5].loc[0,'polarization']=.4
    if fault=='infinite':data[.5].loc[0,'circulation']=np.inf
    with pytest.raises(ValueError,match=error):pairs.pair_rows('test',10,data)


def test_completion_guard_and_hash_manifest(tmp_path):
    stem='10-fish__synthetic';folder=tmp_path/'trials'/stem
    (folder/'tables').mkdir(parents=True)
    data=tables();threshold_summary=[];output_hashes={}
    for threshold,table in data.items():
        path=folder/'tables'/f'collective-threshold-{threshold:g}.csv';table.to_csv(path,index=False)
        output_hashes[str(path.relative_to(folder))]=pairs.digest(path)
        q=pairs.quantiles(table.circulation,'c')
        threshold_summary.append({'threshold_bl_s':threshold,'circulation':{
            'n':q['c_n'],'0.05':q['c_p05'],'0.5':q['c_median'],'0.95':q['c_p95']}})
    summary={'trial':'10-fish/synthetic','fish':10,'quality':{'frames':4},'threshold_sensitivity':threshold_summary}
    (folder/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary))
    output_hashes['summary.json']=pairs.digest(folder/'summary.json')
    (folder/'provenance.json').write_text(json.dumps({'output_hashes':output_hashes}))
    config=tmp_path/'config.json'
    config.write_text(json.dumps({'trials':[stem,'30-fish__missing'],'low_speed_sensitivity_bl_s':[.25,.5,1.]}))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError,match='Missing completed trials'):pairs.run(tmp_path,config)
    assert not (tmp_path/'tables').exists()
    result,manifest=pairs.run(tmp_path,config,allow_partial=True)
    assert len(result)==3
    assert manifest['cohort_complete'] is False
    assert manifest['missing_trials']==['30-fish__missing']
    assert len(manifest['input_hashes'])==5
    assert len(manifest['source_hashes'])==2
    assert manifest['output_hashes']['threshold-pairs.csv']==pairs.digest(tmp_path/'tables/threshold-pairs.csv')
    assert 'Exploratory' in manifest['analysis_status']
    changed=folder/'tables/collective-threshold-0.5.csv'
    changed.write_text(changed.read_text()+'\n')
    with pytest.raises(ValueError,match='output hash mismatch'):pairs.run(tmp_path,config,allow_partial=True)

===== SOURCE tests/test_compare_trial.py | SHA256 9235bfb2f3dd59acf0790d155ef7c48d512e67ad0da2195a87719f404969dbb5 =====
"""Comparison checks use analytic examples, not expected real-trial rankings."""
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from shiners.compare_trial import (
    POSE_INDICES, collective_summary, common_cohort_summaries, file_hash,
    heading_selection, run, threshold_frame_selection, validate_tracks,
)
from shiners.metrics import collective, kinematics


def circular_tracks(fish=4, frames=61):
    t=np.repeat(np.arange(frames)*.1,fish)
    ids=np.tile(np.arange(fish),frames)
    phase=t+ids*2*np.pi/fish
    tr=pd.DataFrame({'frame':np.repeat(np.arange(frames),fish),'id':ids,
                     'time':t,'segment':0,'group':f'{fish}-fish','sequence':'synthetic',
                     'X':2*np.cos(phase),'Y':2*np.sin(phase),
                     'ANGLE':phase+np.pi/2,'body_length':1.})
    for i in POSE_INDICES:
        offset=(10-i)/20
        tr[f'poseX{i}']=tr.X+offset*np.cos(tr.ANGLE)
        tr[f'poseY{i}']=tr.Y+offset*np.sin(tr.ANGLE)
    return tr


def test_quality_accepts_other_fish_counts_and_explicit_gaps():
    tr=circular_tracks(fish=7)
    tr=tr[tr.frame!=30].copy()
    tr.loc[tr.frame>=45,'segment']=1
    qc=validate_tracks(tr)
    assert qc['fish']==7
    assert qc['segment_count']==2
    assert qc['missing_frames_inside_range']==1
    assert [(b['first_frame'],b['last_frame']) for b in qc['continuous_blocks']]==[(0,29),(31,44),(45,60)]


@pytest.mark.parametrize('fault,message',[
    ('duplicate','Duplicate'),('missing','Incomplete'),('nonfinite','Nonfinite'),
    ('length','No positive'),('time','Irregular'),('frame_time','Inconsistent'),
])
def test_quality_rejects_invalid_measurement_inputs(fault,message):
    tr=circular_tracks()
    if fault=='duplicate':tr=pd.concat([tr,tr.iloc[[0]]],ignore_index=True)
    if fault=='missing':tr=tr.iloc[1:]
    if fault=='nonfinite':tr.loc[0,'poseX6']=np.nan
    if fault=='length':tr['body_length']=0
    if fault=='time':tr.loc[tr.frame==25,'time']+=.01
    if fault=='frame_time':tr.loc[0,'time']+=.01
    with pytest.raises(ValueError,match=message):validate_tracks(tr)


def test_quality_discloses_isolated_nonpositive_lengths_without_mutating_data():
    tr=circular_tracks()
    tr.loc[0,'body_length']=0
    tr.loc[8,'body_length']=-1
    qc=validate_tracks(tr)
    assert qc['nonpositive_length_rows']==2
    assert qc['nonpositive_length_frames']==[0,2]
    assert [r['id'] for r in qc['nonpositive_length_observations']]==[0,0]
    assert tr.loc[0,'body_length']==0
    assert tr.loc[8,'body_length']==-1


def test_common_cohort_distinguishes_sampling_from_values():
    a=pd.DataFrame({'frame':[2,4,6],'polarization':[.3,.6,.9],
                    'circulation':[.1,.6,.8],'signed_circulation':[-.1,.6,.8],
                    'eligible_fraction':[1.,1.,1.],'iid_direction_reference':[.1]*3})
    b=a.copy();b.loc[0,'circulation']=np.nan;b.loc[2,'polarization']=np.nan
    assert collective_summary(a)['circulation_median']==.6
    assert collective_summary(b)['circulation_median']==.7
    joint=common_cohort_summaries([a,b],[.25,1.],'threshold_bl_s')
    assert joint['common_frames']==1
    assert joint['common_fraction']==1/3
    assert [s['circulation']['0.5'] for s in joint['settings']]==[.6,.6]
    c_only=common_cohort_summaries([a,b],[.25,1.],'threshold_bl_s',False)
    assert c_only['common_frames']==2
    fixed=threshold_frame_selection(b,[a,b],[.25,1.],1.)
    assert fixed['settings'][0]['candidate_frames']==3
    assert fixed['settings'][0]['baseline_undefined_frames']==1
    assert fixed['settings'][0]['baseline_circulation']['0.5']==.7
    with pytest.raises(ValueError,match='frame ordering'):
        common_cohort_summaries([a,b.iloc[::-1]],[.25,1.],'threshold_bl_s')


def test_leave_one_out_equivalence_and_invariant_rotation():
    tr=circular_tracks(fish=4,frames=1)
    tr['vx']=-.4*np.sin(tr.ANGLE-np.pi/2)
    tr['vy']=.4*np.cos(tr.ANGLE-np.pi/2)
    v=tr[['vx','vy']].to_numpy()
    relative=v-v.mean(axis=0)
    other_mean=(v.sum(axis=0)-v)/(len(v)-1)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(relative,(len(v)-1)/len(v)*(v-other_mean),atol=1e-15)
    assert np.isnan(collective(tr,1,.5).circulation.iloc[0])
    adjusted=collective(tr,1,.5*(len(v)-1)/len(v))
    assert adjusted.circulation.iloc[0]==pytest.approx(1)
    assert adjusted.eligible_fraction.iloc[0]==1
    # Doubling the reference length and halving the threshold preserves C.
    scaled=collective(tr,2,.25*(len(v)-1)/len(v))
    assert scaled.circulation.iloc[0]==pytest.approx(adjusted.circulation.iloc[0])


def test_heading_selection_retains_raw_measurements_and_exposes_coverage():
    tr=circular_tracks()
    tr.loc[(tr.id==0)&(tr.frame>=30),'ANGLE']+=np.pi
    k=kinematics(tr)
    c=collective(k,1)
    frames,report=heading_selection(k,c)
    raw=frames.polarization_raw.to_numpy()
    valid=np.isfinite(c.polarization)
    assert np.isfinite(raw).all()
    np.testing.assert_allclose(raw[valid],c.loc[valid,'polarization'],atol=1e-15)
    assert report['polarization_valid_frames']==49
    assert report['heading_masked_rows']==12
    assert report['heading_jump_rows']==2
    assert report['raw_polarization_on_excluded_frames']['n']==12
    # With 4 fish, 3 valid heads fall below the >=80% rule.
    assert report['affected_fish_only']['valid_frames']==49
    assert frames.loc[valid,'polarization_iid_reference'].iloc[0]==pytest.approx(np.sqrt(np.pi/16))
    json.dumps(report,allow_nan=False)


def test_affected_fish_only_p_retains_frames_when_eighty_percent_valid():
    tr=circular_tracks(fish=5)
    tr.loc[(tr.id==0)&(tr.frame>=30),'ANGLE']+=np.pi
    k=kinematics(tr);c=collective(k,1)
    frames,report=heading_selection(k,c)
    assert report['affected_fish_only']['valid_frames']==61
    assert report['affected_fish_only']['common_frames']==49
    assert frames.heading_valid_fish_count.min()==4
    assert frames.polarization_valid_fish.notna().all()
    assert frames.loc[frames.heading_valid_fish_count==4,'polarization_valid_fish_iid_reference'].iloc[0]==pytest.approx(np.sqrt(np.pi/16))
    np.testing.assert_allclose(frames.loc[c.polarization.notna(),'polarization_valid_fish'],c.polarization.dropna(),atol=1e-15)


def test_track_only_trial_completes_and_preserves_all_frames(tmp_path):

"""Offline checks for bounded split-ZIP fetching. Run with unittest discover."""
import importlib.util
import copy
import io
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch
import zipfile

SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('fetch_pilot', Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]/'scripts'/'fetch_pilot.py')
fetch = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
SPEC.loader.exec_module(fetch)


class MemoryTransport:
    def __init__(self, parts): self.parts = parts; self.calls = []
    def range(self, name, start, end, total):
        data = self.parts[name]
        if len(data) != total: raise ValueError('Wrong part size')
        self.calls.append((name, start, end))
        return data[start:end+1]


def fixture(compression=zipfile.ZIP_STORED):
    data = io.BytesIO()
    payload = b'fish trajectory data\n' * 100
    with zipfile.ZipFile(data, 'w', compression=compression) as z:
        z.writestr('test.parquet', payload)
        z.writestr('unselected.bin', b'do not extract this')
    blob = data.getvalue()
    # Split through payload and central-directory/end records.
    cuts = [0, 39, len(blob)-30, len(blob)-12, len(blob)]
    parts = {f'p{i}': blob[a:b] for i,(a,b) in enumerate(zip(cuts,cuts[1:]))}
    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(blob)) as z:
        infos = z.infolist()
    archive = {'name':'test.zip', 'size':len(blob), 'sha256':'0'*64,
               'parts':[{'name':k,'size':len(v)} for k,v in parts.items()],
               'members':[{'path':i.filename,'size':i.file_size,'compressed_size':i.compress_size,'crc32':f'{i.CRC:08x}'} for i in infos]}
    return archive, MemoryTransport(parts), payload


class RangeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_exact_final_range_required(self):
        headers = 'HTTP/1.1 302 Found\r\nLocation: example\r\n\r\nHTTP/2 206\r\nContent-Range: bytes 3-5/12\r\n\r\n'
        fetch.check_range_response(206, headers, b'abc', 3, 5, 12)
        for status, body, end, total in [(200,b'abc',5,12),(206,b'ab',5,12),(206,b'abc',6,12),(206,b'abc',5,13)]:
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                fetch.check_range_response(status, headers, body, 3, end, total)

    def test_remote_seek_across_parts(self):
        archive, transport, _ = fixture()
        reader = fetch.RemoteArchive(archive, transport)
        joined = b''.join(transport.parts.values())
        reader.seek(31)
        self.assertEqual(reader.read(50), joined[31:81])
        reader.seek(-22, 2)
        self.assertEqual(reader.read(), joined[-22:])
        reader.seek(len(joined)+3)
        self.assertEqual(reader.read(1), b'')
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): reader.seek(-1)

    def test_stored_and_deflated_split_zip(self):
        for compression in [zipfile.ZIP_STORED, zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED]:
            with self.subTest(compression=compression), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
                archive, transport, payload = fixture(compression)
                output = Path(d)/'tracks.parquet'
                result = fetch.fetch_member(archive, 'test.parquet', output, transport)
                self.assertEqual(output.read_bytes(), payload)
                self.assertTrue(result['zip_member_crc32_verified'])
                self.assertFalse(result['full_archive_sha256_verified'])
                self.assertEqual(set(p.name for p in Path(d).iterdir()), {'tracks.parquet'})
                count = len(transport.calls)
                self.assertEqual(fetch.fetch_member(archive,'test.parquet',output,transport,result), result)
                self.assertEqual(count, len(transport.calls), 'Verified rerun should not fetch ranges')
                output.write_bytes(b'corrupted')
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'verified provenance'):
                    fetch.fetch_member(archive,'test.parquet',output,transport,result)

    def test_crc_corruption_does_not_publish(self):
        archive, transport, _ = fixture()
        # Corrupt stored payload while retaining original central-directory CRC.
        name = list(transport.parts)[1]
        part = bytearray(transport.parts[name]); part[20] ^= 1
        transport.parts[name] = bytes(part)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            output=Path(d)/'tracks.parquet'
            with self.assertRaises(zipfile.BadZipFile):
                fetch.fetch_member(archive,'test.parquet',output,transport)
            self.assertFalse(output.exists())
            self.assertEqual(list(Path(d).iterdir()), [])

    def test_manifest_member_mismatch_and_symlink(self):
        archive, transport, _ = fixture()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            output=Path(d)/'tracks.parquet'
            archive['members'][0]['size'] += 1
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'disagree'):
                fetch.fetch_member(archive,'test.parquet',output,transport)
            target=Path(d)/'outside'; target.write_text('preserve')
            output.symlink_to(target)
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'symlink'):
                fetch.fetch_member(archive,'test.parquet',output,transport,force=True)
            self.assertEqual(target.read_text(),'preserve')

    def test_budget_fails_before_http(self):
        transport=fetch.CurlTransport(2)
        with patch.object(fetch.subprocess,'run') as run:
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'budget'):
                transport.range('part',0,2,100)
            run.assert_not_called()

    def test_manifest_archive_and_part_mismatches(self):
        archives = []
        for name, (member, _) in fetch.MEMBERS.items():
            archives.append({'name':name, 'size':10, 'sha256':'a'*64,
                             'parts':[{'name':name, 'size':10}],
                             'members':[{'path':member, 'size':3, 'compressed_size':3, 'crc32':'00000000'}]})
        manifest={'schema_version':1, 'repository':fetch.REPOSITORY,
                  'tag':fetch.TAG, 'archives':archives}
        source={'files':[{'name':a['name'],'size':a['size'],'sha256':a['sha256']} for a in archives]}
        self.assertEqual(set(fetch.validate_manifest(manifest,source)),set(fetch.MEMBERS))
        bad=copy.deepcopy(manifest); bad['archives'][0]['sha256']='b'*64
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'source manifest'):
            fetch.validate_manifest(bad,source)
        bad=copy.deepcopy(manifest); bad['archives'][0]['parts'][0]['size']=9
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'Part sizes'):
            fetch.validate_manifest(bad,source)
        bad=copy.deepcopy(manifest); bad['archives'][0]['parts'][0]['name']='../evil'
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'part names'):
            fetch.validate_manifest(bad,source)
        bad=copy.deepcopy(manifest); bad['archives'][0]['members']*=2
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'duplicated'):
            fetch.validate_manifest(bad,source)

    def test_release_identity_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'identity'):
            fetch.validate_manifest({'schema_version':1,'repository':'wrong','tag':fetch.TAG}, {})


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()

class MemoryTransport:
    def __init__(self, parts):
        self.parts = parts
        self.calls = []
    def range(self, name, start, end, total):
        assert len(self.parts[name]) == total
        self.calls.append((name,start,end))
        return self.parts[name][start:end+1]


def fixture():
    archives=[]; parts={}
    for kind,name in [('tracks','shiners-tracks.zip'),('networks','shiners-networks.zip'),('videos','shiners-videos.zip')]:
        buffer=io.BytesIO()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(buffer,'w',compression=zipfile.ZIP_STORED) as z:
            if kind in fetch.KINDS:
                for trial in fetch.TRIALS:
                    z.writestr(fetch.PREFIXES[kind]+trial+'.parquet',f'{kind} {trial}\n'.encode()*5)
            else:
                z.writestr('unselected-video.mp4',b'no video should be fetched')
        blob=buffer.getvalue();mid=len(blob)//2
        p1=name+'.part001';p2=name+'.part002';parts[p1]=blob[:mid];parts[p2]=blob[mid:]
        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(blob)) as z:
            members=[{'path':i.filename,'size':i.file_size,'compressed_size':i.compress_size,'crc32':f'{i.CRC:08x}'} for i in z.infolist()]
        archives.append({'name':name,'size':len(blob),'sha256':'a'*64,
                         'parts':[{'name':p1,'size':mid},{'name':p2,'size':len(blob)-mid}],
                         'members':members})
    manifest={'schema_version':1,'repository':fetch.helpers.REPOSITORY,'tag':fetch.helpers.TAG,'archives':archives}
    source={'files':[{'name':a['name'],'size':a['size'],'sha256':a['sha256']} for a in archives]}
    return manifest,source,MemoryTransport(parts)

===== SOURCE tests/test_metrics.py | SHA256 b83d2c5f4a29218a56b68007f4d1f7788cceb4b101778846be2b5612edfcf5ef =====
"""Synthetic checks derived from analytic geometry, not real-data expectations."""

import unittest
import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from shiners.metrics import kinematics, curvature, collective, spatial, visibility, heading_diagnostics


def trajectory(n=61, dt=.1):
    t = np.arange(n)*dt
    return pd.DataFrame({"frame": np.arange(n), "id": 0, "segment": 0,
                         "time": t, "X": 3*t, "Y": 4*t, "ANGLE": 0.})


def frame(x, y, theta=None, vx=None, vy=None):
    n = len(x)
    return pd.DataFrame({"frame": 0, "time": 0., "segment": 0, "id": np.arange(n),
                         "X": x, "Y": y, "ANGLE": np.zeros(n) if theta is None else theta,
                         "vx": np.zeros(n) if vx is None else vx, "vy": np.zeros(n) if vy is None else vy})


def midline(x, y):
    return pd.DataFrame({**{f"poseX{i}": [v] for i, v in enumerate(x)},
                         **{f"poseY{i}": [v] for i, v in enumerate(y)},
                         "poseX21": [1e9], "poseY21": [-1e9]})


class KinematicsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_constant_velocity_and_preserved_index(self):
        tr = trajectory().sample(frac=1, random_state=1)
        out = kinematics(tr)
        self.assertTrue(out.index.equals(tr.index))
        valid = out.frame.between(6, 54)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(out.loc[valid, "vx"], 3, atol=1e-10)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(out.loc[valid, "vy"], 4, atol=1e-10)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(out.loc[valid, "ax"], 0, atol=1e-9)
        self.assertTrue(out.loc[~valid, ["vx", "vy", "ax", "ay", "turn_rate"]].isna().all().all())

    def test_acceleration_and_wrapped_signed_turn(self):
        tr = trajectory()
        tr["X"] = 2*tr.time**2 + 3*tr.time
        tr["ANGLE"] = (3 + .7*tr.time + np.pi) % (2*np.pi) - np.pi
        out = kinematics(tr)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(out.ax.dropna(), 4, atol=1e-9)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(out.turn_rate.dropna(), .7, atol=1e-10)

    def test_gaps_and_segment_boundaries_never_bridge(self):
        tr = trajectory(100)
        tr = tr[tr.frame != 40].copy()
        tr.loc[tr.frame > 40, "X"] += 1000
        tr.loc[tr.frame >= 70, "segment"] = 1
        out = kinematics(tr)
        for center in [40, 70]:
            # Extra sample removes noisy block-edge data from retained windows.
            affected = out.frame.between(center-6, center+5)
            self.assertTrue(out.loc[affected, "vx"].isna().all())
        np.testing.assert_allclose(out.vx.dropna(), 3, atol=1e-9)

    def test_irregular_sampling_is_rejected_even_short_block(self):
        tr = trajectory(8)
        tr.loc[4, "time"] += .01
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Irregular"):
            kinematics(tr)

    def test_heading_jump_contaminates_only_heading_metrics_and_sg_support(self):
        tr = trajectory()
        tr.loc[tr.frame >= 30, "ANGLE"] = np.pi
        tr["poseX0"] = tr.X+1; tr["poseX20"] = tr.X-1
        tr["poseY0"] = tr.Y; tr["poseY20"] = tr.Y
        out = kinematics(tr)
        self.assertEqual(out.loc[out.heading_jump, "frame"].tolist(), [29, 30])
        self.assertEqual(out.loc[~out.heading_valid, "frame"].tolist(), list(range(24, 36)))
        self.assertTrue(out.loc[~out.heading_valid, "turn_rate"].isna().all())
        self.assertTrue(out.loc[~out.heading_valid, "vx"].notna().all())
        self.assertTrue(out.heading_valid.iloc[0])  # A kinematic edge is not a bad heading.
        self.assertAlmostEqual(abs(out.heading_axis_error.iloc[40]), np.pi)
        organized = collective(out, 1)
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(organized.polarization.iloc[29]))
        self.assertEqual(organized.polarization.iloc[0], 1)


class CurvatureTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_straight_line_and_degenerate_curve(self):
        np.testing.assert_allclose(curvature(midline(np.linspace(0, 20, 21), np.zeros(21))), 0, atol=1e-12)
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(curvature(midline(np.ones(21), np.ones(21)))[0]))

    def test_circular_arc_sign_and_translation(self):
        angle = np.linspace(-.3, .3, 21)
        # Increasing angle on an image-coordinate circle is clockwise.
        for radius in [10., 100.]:
            tr = midline(1000+radius*np.cos(angle), 2000+radius*np.sin(angle))
            self.assertAlmostEqual(curvature(tr)[0], 1/radius, delta=1e-3/radius)
            reflected = midline(1000+radius*np.cos(angle), 2000-radius*np.sin(angle))
            self.assertAlmostEqual(curvature(reflected)[0], -1/radius, delta=1e-3/radius)


class CollectiveTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_parallel_translation_is_aligned_but_circulation_undefined(self):
        tr = frame([-1, 1], [0, 0], vx=[3, 3], vy=[4, 4])
        out = collective(tr, 2).iloc[0]
        self.assertEqual(out.polarization, 1)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out.spread_bl, .5)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out.centroid_speed_bl_s, 2.5)
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(out.circulation))
        self.assertEqual(out.eligible_fraction, 0)

    def test_circular_motion_and_translation_invariance(self):
        a = np.arange(8)*2*np.pi/8
        tr = frame(5*np.cos(a), 5*np.sin(a), theta=a+np.pi/2,
                   vx=-2*np.sin(a), vy=2*np.cos(a))
        out = collective(tr, 1).iloc[0]
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out.circulation, 1)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out.signed_circulation, 1)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out.iid_direction_reference, np.sqrt(1/(8*np.pi)))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out.polarization, 0, delta=1e-12)
        tr["vx"] += 20; tr["vy"] -= 7
        self.assertAlmostEqual(collective(tr, 1).circulation.iloc[0], 1)
        tr["vx"] *= -1; tr["vy"] *= -1
        reversed_out = collective(tr, 1).iloc[0]
        self.assertAlmostEqual(reversed_out.signed_circulation, -1)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(reversed_out.circulation, 1)

    def test_invalid_velocity_and_insufficient_eligibility(self):
        tr = frame([-1, 1], [0, 0], vx=[0, 0], vy=[1, -1])
        tr.loc[0, "vx"] = np.nan
        out = collective(tr, 1).iloc[0]
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(out.circulation))
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(out.centroid_speed_bl_s))
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(out.eligible_fraction))
        tr = frame([0, 1, -1], [0, 0, 0], vy=[0, 1, -1])
        out = collective(tr, 1).iloc[0]
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out.eligible_fraction, 2/3)
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(out.circulation))


class SpatialVisibilityTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_known_body_frame_direction_and_normalization(self):
        # Fish 0 points down: displacement (2,1) is forward=1, right=-2.
        tr = frame([0, 2], [0, 1], theta=[np.pi/2, 0])
        out = spatial(tr, 1, extent=4, bins=8)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out["density"].sum(), 1)
        self.assertEqual(out["focal_count"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(out["shown_pair_fraction"], 1)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(out["nearest"].distance_bl, np.sqrt(5))
        self.assertEqual(out["histogram"][5, 2], 1)
        # The reverse pair seen by fish 1 has forward=-2, right=-1.
        self.assertEqual(out["histogram"][2, 3], 1)

    def test_out_of_view_pairs_do_not_change_focal_denominator(self):
        tr = frame([0, 1, 20], [0, 0, 0])
        out = spatial(tr, 1, extent=2, bins=4)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out["shown_pair_fraction"], 2/6)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out["density"].sum(), 2/3)

    def test_visibility_zero_degree_and_unknown_frame(self):
        tr = pd.concat([frame([0, 1, 2], [0, 0, 0]), frame([0, 1, 2], [0, 0, 0]).assign(frame=1)], ignore_index=True)
        net = pd.DataFrame({"frame": [0, 0, 0], "id1": [0, 1, 1], "id2": [1, 0, 2]})
        out = visibility(tr, net)
        self.assertEqual(out["degree"].degree.tolist(), [1, 2, 0])
        self.assertEqual(out["degree"].frame.unique().tolist(), [0])
        self.assertEqual(out["per_frame"].mean_degree.iloc[0], 1)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out["reciprocal_edge_fraction"], 2/3)
        dangling = net.copy()
        dangling.loc[0, "id2"] = 99
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Dangling"):
            visibility(tr, dangling)


class HeadingDiagnosticTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_flip_then_unflip_exposes_sustained_reverse_interval(self):
        tr = trajectory(100)
        tr["Y"] = 0.
        tr.loc[tr.frame.between(30, 69), "ANGLE"] = np.pi
        k = kinematics(tr)
        out = heading_diagnostics(k, 1)
        self.assertEqual([(x["prev_frame"], x["frame"]) for x in out["heading_events"]], [(29, 30), (69, 70)])
        self.assertEqual(out["speed_eligible_rows_before_heading_mask"], 88)
        self.assertEqual(out["reverse_motion_rows"], 40)
        self.assertGreater(out["reverse_motion_rows_outside_jump_mask"], 0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(out["reverse_motion_fraction"], 40/88)
        self.assertEqual(out["longest_reverse_runs_per_fish"], [{"id": 0, "start": 30, "end": 69, "segment": 0, "n": 40}])
        json.dumps(out, allow_nan=False)

    def test_gaps_segments_and_ineligible_rows_break_reverse_runs(self):
        # Explicit kinematics lets the test isolate run boundaries from SG trim.
        tr = trajectory(20).assign(ANGLE=np.pi, vx=1., vy=0.)
        tr = tr[tr.frame != 5].copy()
        tr.loc[tr.frame >= 12, "segment"] = 1
        tr.loc[tr.frame == 17, "vx"] = np.nan
        out = heading_diagnostics(tr, 1)
        self.assertEqual(out["longest_reverse_runs_per_fish"], [{"id": 0, "start": 6, "end": 11, "segment": 0, "n": 6}])
        # A heading change across the gap must not be described as a one-frame jump.
        tr.loc[tr.frame < 5, "ANGLE"] = 0
        self.assertEqual(heading_diagnostics(tr, 1)["heading_events"], [])

    def test_no_speed_eligible_data_is_json_safe(self):
        tr = trajectory(5).assign(vx=np.nan, vy=np.nan)
        out = heading_diagnostics(tr, 1)
        self.assertIsNone(out["reverse_motion_fraction"])
        self.assertEqual(out["longest_reverse_runs_per_fish"][0]["n"], 0)
        json.dumps(out, allow_nan=False)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

===== SOURCE tests/test_network_summary.py | SHA256 d22231a9c13759ed1477304f2f035dc11b7209792c1f55b897879f4dee9eff85 =====
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import pytest

from shiners.metrics import visibility
from shiners.network_summary import summarize_network


def tracks_fixture():
    return pd.DataFrame([
        {'frame': frame, 'id': fish, 'X': float(index*3), 'Y': float(index*4 + frame)}
        for frame in [2, 4, 8] for index, fish in enumerate([10, 20, 40])
    ])


def edges_fixture(tracks):
    # Deliberately interleave frame order and produce repeated byte indices.
    keys = [(4, 20, 40), (2, 10, 20), (4, 40, 20), (2, 20, 10), (4, 10, 20)]
    xy = tracks.set_index(['frame', 'id'])[['X', 'Y']]
    return pd.DataFrame([
        {'frame': f, 'id1': a, 'id2': b, 'n_rays': i+1,
         'angular_size_deg': .36*(i+1),
         'distance': float(np.linalg.norm(xy.loc[(f,a)]-xy.loc[(f,b)]))}
        for i, (f, a, b) in enumerate(keys)
    ])


def save(tmp_path, df):
    path = tmp_path/'network.parquet'
    df.to_parquet(path, index=False)
    return path


@pytest.mark.parametrize('batch_size', [1, 2, 3, 100])
def test_exact_unsorted_summary_matches_small_reference(tmp_path, batch_size):
    tracks = tracks_fixture().sample(frac=1, random_state=7)
    network = edges_fixture(tracks)
    result = summarize_network(save(tmp_path, network), tracks, tmp_path/'out', batch_size)
    reference = visibility(tracks, network)
    assert result['network_rows'] == 5
    assert result['covered_frame_count'] == 2
    assert result['network_uncovered_frames'] == [8]
    assert result['observer_frame_count'] == 6
    assert result['visible_degree_mean'] == pytest.approx(reference['degree'].degree.mean())
    assert result['visible_fraction_mean'] == pytest.approx(5/12)
    assert result['reciprocal_edge_fraction'] == pytest.approx(reference['reciprocal_edge_fraction'])
    assert result['reciprocal_edge_fraction'] == .8
    assert result['degree_histogram'] == {'degree': [0,1,2], 'count': [1,5,0]}
    assert sum(result['angular_size_histogram']['count']) == len(network)
    assert result['processing']['packed_adjacency_bytes'] == 6  # 3 frames x ceil(9/8)
    assert result['quality']['max_network_distance_error_px'] == 0
    matched = result['matched_duration']
    assert matched['tracked_frame_count'] == 3
    assert matched['frame_start'] == 2
    assert matched['frame_end'] == 8
    assert matched['coverage_fraction'] == pytest.approx(2/3)
    for key in ['network_rows', 'covered_frame_count', 'network_uncovered_frames',
                'observer_frame_count', 'visible_degree_mean', 'visible_fraction_mean',
                'reciprocal_edge_fraction']:
        assert matched[key] == result[key]
    frame = pd.read_csv(tmp_path/'out/per_frame.csv')
    assert frame.frame.tolist() == [2,4,8]
    assert frame.mean_degree.iloc[:2].tolist() == pytest.approx([2/3, 1])
    assert frame.reciprocal_edge_fraction.iloc[:2].tolist() == pytest.approx([1, 2/3])
    assert np.isnan(frame.mean_degree.iloc[2])
    assert np.isnan(frame.reciprocal_edge_fraction.iloc[2])
    json.dumps(result, allow_nan=False)


@pytest.mark.parametrize('batch_size', [1, 100])
def test_duplicate_edges_rejected_across_or_inside_batches(tmp_path, batch_size):
    tracks = tracks_fixture()
    network = edges_fixture(tracks)
    network = pd.concat([network, network.iloc[[0]]], ignore_index=True)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match='Duplicate visibility edges'):
        summarize_network(save(tmp_path, network), tracks, batch_size=batch_size)

    ('frame', 100, 'Dangling'), ('id1', 999, 'Dangling'), ('id2', 30, 'Dangling'),
    ('id2', 20, 'Self'), ('frame', 2.5, 'noninteger'), ('id1', np.inf, 'nonfinite'),
    ('n_rays', 0, 'Nonpositive'), ('n_rays', 1.5, 'noninteger'),

def test_matched_duration_uses_observed_frame_order_and_pooled_edges(tmp_path):
    # Gapped IDs, shuffled input, and unknown coverage do not change the cutoff.
    frames = 10 + 3*np.arange(18001)
    tracks = pd.DataFrame({'frame': np.repeat(frames, 2),
                           'id': np.tile([10, 20], len(frames)),
                           'X': np.tile([0., 5.], len(frames)), 'Y': 0.})
    tracks = tracks.sample(frac=1, random_state=7)
    network = pd.DataFrame({
        'frame': [frames[17999], frames[0], frames[17998], frames[0], frames[17999]],
        'id1': [10, 10, 10, 20, 20], 'id2': [20, 20, 20, 10, 10],
        'n_rays': 1, 'angular_size_deg': .36, 'distance': 5.,
    })
    result = summarize_network(save(tmp_path, network), tracks, batch_size=2)
    matched = result['matched_duration']
    assert matched['tracked_frame_count'] == 17999
    assert matched['target_frame_count'] == 17999
    assert matched['frame_end'] == int(frames[17998])
    assert matched['covered_frame_count'] == 2
    assert matched['coverage_fraction'] == pytest.approx(2/17999)
    assert matched['network_uncovered_frames'] == frames[1:17998].tolist()
    assert matched['network_rows'] == 3
    assert matched['observer_frame_count'] == 4
    assert matched['visible_degree_mean'] == .75
    assert matched['visible_fraction_mean'] == .75
    assert matched['reciprocal_edge_fraction'] == pytest.approx(2/3)
    assert result['network_rows'] == 5
    assert result['reciprocal_edge_fraction'] == .8
    json.dumps(result, allow_nan=False)


def test_float32_geometry_and_angular_tolerances(tmp_path):
    tracks = tracks_fixture(); network = edges_fixture(tracks)
    tracks['X'] = tracks.X.astype('float32')
    network['distance'] = (network.distance + .0005).astype('float32')
    network['angular_size_deg'] = network.angular_size_deg.astype('float32')
    result = summarize_network(save(tmp_path, network), tracks)
    assert result['quality']['distance_tolerance_px'] == .001
    assert result['quality']['angular_tolerance_deg'] == .0001


def test_high_angular_values_record_histogram_overflow(tmp_path):
    tracks = tracks_fixture(); network = edges_fixture(tracks)
    # Preserve the exact documented ray formula while ensuring no dropped counts.
    network.loc[0, ['n_rays','angular_size_deg']] = [2001, .36*2001]
    result = summarize_network(save(tmp_path, network), tracks)
    hist = result['angular_size_histogram']
    assert hist['overflow'] == 1
    assert sum(hist['count']) + hist['overflow'] + hist['underflow'] == len(network)


def test_track_contract_and_arguments(tmp_path):

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match='Duplicate track'):
        summarize_network(path, pd.concat([tracks,tracks.iloc[[0]]]))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match='Incomplete fish set'):

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match='batch_size'):
        summarize_network(path, tracks, batch_size=0)

import copy

from pathlib import Path

spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('plot_comparison',Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]/'scripts/plot_comparison.py')
plot=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec);spec.loader.exec_module(plot)


def q(values):
    a=np.asarray(values,dtype=float);a=a[np.isfinite(a)]
    return {'n':len(a),**{str(p):float(np.quantile(a,p)) if len(a) else None for p in [.05,.5,.95]}}


def fixture(stem=plot.TRIALS[0]):
    n=int(stem.split('-fish')[0]);n=151 if n==150 else n
    c=pd.DataFrame({'frame':[1,2,3,5,6,7],'time':[1,2,3,5,6,7],
                    'segment':[0,0,0,1,1,1],'polarization':[.8,.9,np.nan,.6,.7,.8],
                    'circulation':[np.nan,.2,.3,np.nan,.6,.9],
                    'eligible_fraction':[np.nan,.8,.9,.6,.9,1.],
                    'polarization_valid_fish':[.8,.9,.4,.6,.7,.8]})
    cq=q(c.circulation);pq=q(c.polarization)
    degree_count=[0]*n;degree_count[1]=n*3;degree_count[2]=n*3
    summary={'trial':stem.replace('__','/'),'group':stem.split('__')[0],
             'sequence':stem.split('__')[1],'fish':n,'length_scale_px':40.,
             'quality':{'frames':6,'duration_s':6.,'segment_count':2},
             **{key:q([1,2,3]) for key in plot.METRICS},
             'polarization':pq,'circulation':cq,'circulation_eligible_frame_fraction':4/6,
             'joint_eligible_frame_fraction':3/6,
             'threshold_sensitivity':[{'threshold_bl_s':t,'circulation':cq,
                'circulation_eligible_frame_fraction':4/6} for t in [.25,.5,1.]],
             'threshold_common_eligible':{'common_frames':3,'common_fraction':.5,
                'settings':[{'threshold_bl_s':t,'circulation':q([.2,.6,.9])} for t in [.25,.5,1.]]},
             'threshold_circulation_common_eligible':{'common_frames':4,'common_fraction':4/6,
                'settings':[{'threshold_bl_s':t,'circulation':cq} for t in [.25,.5,1.]]},
             'threshold_frame_selection':{'baseline_threshold_bl_s':.5,
                'settings':[{'threshold_frame_set_bl_s':t,'candidate_frames':4,'baseline_valid_frames':4,
                             'baseline_undefined_frames':0,'baseline_circulation':cq} for t in [.25,.5,1.]]},
             'leave_one_out_threshold_sensitivity':{'effective_all_mean_cutoff_bl_s':.5*(n-1)/n,

    return {'stem':stem,'summary':summary,'collective':c}


class PlotComparisonTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_counts_quantiles_and_coverage_must_match(self):
        r=fixture();plot.validate_trial(r['stem'],r['summary'],r['collective'])
        for key,value in [('circulation_eligible_frame_fraction',1),('joint_eligible_frame_fraction',1)]:
            s=copy.deepcopy(r['summary']);s[key]=value
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'coverage mismatch'):
                plot.validate_trial(r['stem'],s,r['collective'])
        s=copy.deepcopy(r['summary']);s['polarization']['0.5']=.5
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):plot.validate_trial(r['stem'],s,r['collective'])
        s=copy.deepcopy(r['summary']);s['network']['degree_histogram']['count'][1]-=1
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'denominator mismatch'):
            plot.validate_trial(r['stem'],s,r['collective'])

    def test_histogram_quantiles_match_numpy_interpolation(self):
        net={'fish':10,'degree_histogram':{'degree':[0,1,2,3,4],'count':[0,2,0,3,1]}}
        result=plot.degree_quantiles(net)
        expected=np.quantile(np.repeat([0,1,2,3,4],[0,2,0,3,1])/9,[.05,.5,.95])
        np.testing.assert_allclose([result[k] for k in plot.QKEYS],expected)
        self.assertEqual(result['n'],6)

    def test_threshold_nesting_identities_are_checked(self):
        r=fixture();s=r['summary']
        # Count checks alone would not catch this plausible changed median.
        s['threshold_frame_selection']['settings'][0]['baseline_circulation']=q([.2,.4,.6,.9])
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'baseline 0.25/0.5 identity'):
            plot.validate_trial(r['stem'],s,r['collective'])
        r=fixture();s=r['summary'];selection=s['threshold_frame_selection']['settings'][-1]
        selection.update(baseline_undefined_frames=1,baseline_valid_frames=3,baseline_circulation=q([.2,.6,.9]))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'nested baseline undefined-frame identity'):
            plot.validate_trial(r['stem'],s,r['collective'])
        r=fixture();s=r['summary'];common=s['threshold_circulation_common_eligible']
        common.update(common_frames=3,common_fraction=.5)
        for item in common['settings']:item['circulation']=q([.2,.6,.9])
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'common circulation set'):
            plot.validate_trial(r['stem'],s,r['collective'])

    def test_velocity_denominator_and_added_heading_frames_are_exported(self):
        r=fixture();tables=plot.make_tables([r]);row=tables['trials'].iloc[0]
        self.assertEqual(row.velocity_defined_frames,5)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(row.velocity_defined_frame_fraction,5/6)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(row.circulation_eligible_fraction_of_velocity_defined_frames,4/5)
        self.assertEqual(row.polarization_valid_fish_added_frames,1)
        self.assertEqual(row.polarization_valid_fish_on_added_frames_n,1)
        self.assertEqual(row.polarization_valid_fish_on_added_frames_median,.4)
        r['collective'].loc[2,'polarization_valid_fish']=np.nan
        row=plot.make_tables([r])['trials'].iloc[0]
        self.assertEqual(row.polarization_valid_fish_added_frames,0)
        self.assertIsNone(row.polarization_valid_fish_on_added_frames_median)

    def test_timeline_breaks_at_segments_gaps_and_metric_nans(self):
        r=fixture();x,y=plot.line_with_breaks(r['collective'],'polarization')
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(x[3]));self.assertTrue(np.isnan(y[3]))
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(y[2]))
        np.testing.assert_allclose(x[np.isfinite(x)]*60,r['collective'].time)
        # Even consecutive frame numbers must break at a segment boundary.
        c=r['collective'].copy();c['frame']=[1,2,3,4,5,6]
        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(plot.line_with_breaks(c,'polarization')[0][3]))

    def test_missing_trials_require_explicit_partial_mode(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            root=Path(d);r=fixture();dest=root/'trials'/r['stem'];dest.mkdir(parents=True)
            (dest/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(r['summary']))
            r['collective'].to_csv(dest/'collective.csv',index=False)
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError,'Comparison incomplete'):plot.load_trials(root)
            records,missing=plot.load_trials(root,True)
            self.assertEqual(len(records),1);self.assertEqual(len(missing),9)

    def test_tables_and_all_four_figures_with_ten_synthetic_trials(self):
        records=[fixture(stem) for stem in plot.TRIALS]
        tables=plot.make_tables(records)
        self.assertEqual(len(tables['trials']),10)
        self.assertEqual(len(tables['thresholds']),30)
        self.assertEqual(tables['trials'].iloc[-1].fish,151)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(tables['trials'].iloc[0].visible_fraction_median,1.5/9)
        self.assertTrue((tables['thresholds'].common_subset_circulation_n==4).all())
        self.assertTrue((tables['thresholds'].joint_common_subset_circulation_n==3).all())
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            directory=Path(d)
            plot.plot_alignment(tables,directory)
            plot.plot_thresholds(tables,directory)
            plot.plot_timelines(records,directory)
            plot.plot_chapters(tables,directory)
            self.assertEqual(len(list(directory.glob('*.png'))),4)
            self.assertEqual(len(list(directory.glob('*.svg'))),4)
            self.assertTrue(all(p.stat().st_size>1000 for p in directory.iterdir()))

    def test_geometry_counts_and_complete_nested_sensitivities_are_exported(self):
        r=fixture();s=r['summary']
        s['quality'].update(nonpositive_length_rows=2,nonpositive_length_frame_count=1)
        s['nonpositive_length_frame_exclusion_sensitivity']={
            'removed_frames':[3],'recomputed':{'circulation':q([.2,.6])}}
        s['network']['nonpositive_length_frame_exclusion_sensitivity']={
            'excluded_frame_count':1,'visible_fraction_mean':.2}
        s['network']['matched_duration']={'frames':4,'visible_fraction_mean':.3}
        tables=plot.make_tables([r]);row=tables['trials'].iloc[0]
        self.assertEqual(row.nonpositive_length_rows,2)
        self.assertEqual(row.nonpositive_length_frame_count,1)
        diagnostics=tables['sensitivity'].set_index(['family','parameter'])['value']
        self.assertEqual(diagnostics.loc[('nonpositive_length_frame_exclusion_sensitivity','removed_frames.0')],3)
        self.assertEqual(diagnostics.loc[('nonpositive_length_frame_exclusion_sensitivity','recomputed.circulation.n')],2)
        self.assertEqual(diagnostics.loc[('network_nonpositive_length_frame_exclusion_sensitivity','excluded_frame_count')],1)
        self.assertEqual(diagnostics.loc[('network_matched_duration','visible_fraction_mean')],.3)
        old=plot.make_tables([fixture()])['trials'].iloc[0]
        self.assertIsNone(old.nonpositive_length_rows)

===== SOURCE tests/test_run_comparison.py | SHA256 a17a5804efa769d185b67e09a912db596e947057555b5cadd332a32643710d40 =====
"""Offline orchestration checks; subprocesses and waits are mocked."""
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys

import pytest


spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('run_comparison', Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]/'scripts/run_comparison.py')
runner = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(runner)
TRIAL = '10-fish__0066'


def write_json(path, value):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value))


def ready_inputs(data):
    data.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    files = {}
    for name in runner.INPUT_MEMBERS:
        (data/name).write_bytes(name.encode())
        files[name] = {'sha256': runner.file_hash(data/name), 'size': (data/name).stat().st_size}
    write_json(data/'provenance.json', {'files': files})


def completed(tmp_path):
    repo = tmp_path/'repo'
    config = repo/'config.json'
    write_json(config, {'trials': [TRIAL]})
    data = repo/'data'/TRIAL
    ready_inputs(data)
    output = repo/'out'/TRIAL
    write_json(output/'summary.json', {'trial': '10-fish/0066', 'network': {'network_rows': 1}})
    source_paths = [config]
    for name in ['compare_trial.py', 'metrics.py', 'network_summary.py']:
        path = repo/'src/shiners'/name
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(name)
        source_paths.append(path)
    provenance = {
        'input_hashes': {str(data/name): runner.file_hash(data/name)
                         for name in (*runner.INPUT_MEMBERS, 'provenance.json')},
        'source_hashes': {str(p.relative_to(repo)): runner.file_hash(p) for p in source_paths},
        'output_hashes': {'summary.json': runner.file_hash(output/'summary.json')},
        'fetch_member_hashes_match': True,
    }
    write_json(output/'provenance.json', provenance)
    return repo, config, data, output, provenance


def test_fresh_processes_follow_config_order_and_selection(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    config = tmp_path/'config.json'
    trials = [TRIAL, '30-fish__0084']
    write_json(config, {'trials': trials})
    for trial in trials:
        ready_inputs(tmp_path/'data'/trial)
    calls = []
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner.subprocess, 'run', lambda args, **kw: calls.append((args, kw)))
    runner.run(config, tmp_path/'data', tmp_path/'out')
    assert len(calls) == 2
    for (args, kw), trial in zip(calls, trials):
        assert args == [sys.executable, '-m', 'shiners.compare_trial', '--data', str(tmp_path/'data'/trial),
                        '--output', str(tmp_path/'out'/trial), '--config', str(config)]
        assert kw == {'cwd': runner.ROOT, 'check': True}
    calls.clear()
    runner.run(config, tmp_path/'data', tmp_path/'out', trials=[trials[1], trials[1]])
    assert len(calls) == 1
    assert calls[0][0][4].endswith(trials[1])


def test_waits_until_ready_announces_only_once(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    config = tmp_path/'config.json'
    write_json(config, {'trials': [TRIAL]})
    readiness = iter([False, False, True])
    sleeps, calls = [], []
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, 'downloads_ready', lambda _: next(readiness))
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner.time, 'sleep', sleeps.append)
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner.subprocess, 'run', lambda *args, **kw: calls.append(args))
    runner.run(config, tmp_path/'data', tmp_path/'out', wait_for_downloads=True)
    assert sleeps == [10, 10]
    assert len(calls) == 1
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.count('waiting for') == 1


def test_ready_requires_both_members_and_completed_entries(tmp_path):
    data = tmp_path/TRIAL
    assert not runner.downloads_ready(data)
    ready_inputs(data)
    assert runner.downloads_ready(data)
    provenance = json.loads((data/'provenance.json').read_text())
    provenance['files'].pop('networks.parquet')
    write_json(data/'provenance.json', provenance)
    assert not runner.downloads_ready(data)
    ready_inputs(data)
    (data/'networks.parquet').write_bytes(b'short')
    assert not runner.downloads_ready(data)


def test_resume_checks_all_manifests_then_skips(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    repo, config, data, output, _ = completed(tmp_path)
    validate = runner.validate_completed
    hashed = []
    actual_hash = runner.file_hash
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, 'file_hash', lambda path: hashed.append(path) or actual_hash(path))
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, 'validate_completed', lambda o, d, c: validate(o, d, c, repo))
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner.subprocess, 'run', lambda *a, **k: pytest.fail('Completed trial must not run'))
    runner.run(config, data.parent, output.parent, resume=True)
    assert len(hashed) == 8  # Three inputs, four sources, one output.
    assert 'verified complete; skipping' in capsys.readouterr().out


@pytest.mark.parametrize('category', ['input_hashes', 'source_hashes', 'output_hashes'])
def test_resume_rejects_each_kind_of_changed_file(tmp_path, category):
    repo, config, data, output, provenance = completed(tmp_path)
    name = next(iter(provenance[category]))
    root = output if category == 'output_hashes' else repo
    path = runner._resolve_recorded(name, root)
    path.write_bytes(path.read_bytes()+b'changed')
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=category):
        runner.validate_completed(output, data, config, repo)


def test_resume_rejects_partial_or_untracked_outputs_without_changes(tmp_path):
    repo, config, data, output, _ = completed(tmp_path)
    extra = output/'unexpected.csv'
    extra.write_text('partial')
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match='unrecorded'):
        runner.validate_completed(output, data, config, repo)
    assert extra.read_text() == 'partial'
    (output/'summary.json').unlink()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match='Partial output'):
        runner.validate_completed(output, data, config, repo)


def test_nonempty_output_requires_resume_and_missing_downloads_fail(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _, config, data, output, _ = completed(tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner.subprocess, 'run', lambda *a, **k: pytest.fail('Must not run'))
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match='Nonempty output'):
        runner.run(config, data.parent, output.parent)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match='incomplete'):
        runner.run(config, tmp_path/'missing', tmp_path/'fresh')
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match='--trial'):
        runner.run(config, data.parent, output.parent, trials=['70-fish__0103'])


def test_child_failure_stops_later_trials(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    config = tmp_path/'config.json'
    write_json(config, {'trials': [TRIAL, '30-fish__0084']})
    ready_inputs(tmp_path/'data'/TRIAL)
    calls = []
    def fail(args, **kwargs):
        calls.append(args)
        raise subprocess.CalledProcessError(1, args)
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner.subprocess, 'run', fail)
    with pytest.raises(subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        runner.run(config, tmp_path/'data', tmp_path/'out')
    assert len(calls) == 1
